items.title_zh: 重新思考2型糖尿病：遗传、生活方式与治疗新纪元
items.summary_zh: 本文探讨了2型糖尿病的机制，强调其与体重增加和内脏脂肪（adipose tissue）的积累密切相关。科学家指出，尽管2型糖尿病患者通常能够产生足够的胰岛素，但体重增加导致的多余脂肪会渗入肝脏和胰腺，进而影响胰岛素的功能。这一观点强调了体重管理在2型糖尿病治疗中的重要性，提示我们在应对这一疾病时需要关注生活方式的改变和遗传因素的影响。
items.l1_lead: 2型糖尿病与体重增加和内脏脂肪密切相关，强调体重管理和生活方式改变在治疗中的重要性。
items.l2_summary:
本文探讨了2型糖尿病（Type 2 Diabetes）的机制，强调其与体重增加和内脏脂肪（adipose tissue）的积累密切相关。研究表明，尽管2型糖尿病患者通常能够产生足够的胰岛素（insulin），但体重增加所导致的多余脂肪会渗入肝脏和胰腺，进而影响胰岛素的功能。这一发现提示我们，体重管理在2型糖尿病的治疗中至关重要，尤其是在当前全球范围内，2型糖尿病的发病率持续上升的背景下。

科学家们指出，内脏脂肪的过度积累不仅会导致胰岛素抵抗（insulin resistance），还会引发一系列代谢紊乱，进一步加重糖尿病的病情。因此，控制体重、改善饮食习惯和增加身体活动成为了应对2型糖尿病的重要策略。此外，遗传因素也在2型糖尿病的发病机制中扮演着重要角色，某些基因的变异可能使个体更易于发展为糖尿病。

综上所述，本文强调了在应对2型糖尿病时，除了药物治疗外，生活方式的改变和对遗传因素的关注同样不可忽视。通过综合管理体重和改善生活方式，患者可以有效降低糖尿病的风险，改善健康状况，进入一个新的治疗纪元。

items.l2_summary:
本文探讨了2型糖尿病（Type 2 Diabetes）的发病机制，强调了性别和种族在体重增加后发展糖尿病风险方面的显著差异。研究表明，平均男性在体重增加后发展糖尿病所需的体重增加量低于平均女性，而平均亚洲人所需的体重增加量又低于平均白人。这一现象反映了遗传和生理差异对糖尿病风险的影响，提示在制定预防和治疗策略时应充分考虑这些因素。

具体而言，男性和女性在体重增加后的代谢反应存在差异，可能导致男性在较小的体重增加下就面临更高的糖尿病风险。此外，种族差异也表明，不同人群在体重增加后对糖尿病的易感性不同，亚洲人群在体重增加后更容易发展为糖尿病，这可能与其遗传背景和生理特征有关。

通过对这些差异的深入理解，未来的治疗方法可能会更加个性化和有效。个性化治疗不仅可以提高治疗效果，还能更好地满足不同人群的需求，从而在更大程度上降低糖尿病的发病率。因此，研究者呼吁在糖尿病的预防和治疗策略中，必须考虑性别和种族等因素，以制定更为精准的干预措施。这一研究为2型糖尿病的管理提供了新的视角，强调了个体差异在疾病发展中的重要性。

items.claim_zh: 曼城俱乐部的财务违规判决虽然严重，但不能导致俱乐部的存在被剥夺。
items.article_body:
Manchester City fans are still processing Tuesday’s ruling that the most dominant Premier League team in recent times had, in fact, been found guilty of systematic financial breaches for nearly a decade to help boost its unprecedented era of success. Kevin Parker, a fan for more than 50 years, has faith the club’s Emirati ownership, which has turned City into a soccer powerhouse, will successfully clear its name. David Mooney, another longtime City fan, who runs popular podcasts about the club, describes himself as angry and conflicted. He is worried about what happens should the findings be upheld on appeal and just hopes it will remain in existence.
FILE - Manchester City fans wave the team's flag prior to the League Cup soccer match final between Aston Villa and Manchester City, at Wembley stadium, in London, England, Sunday, March 1, 2020.
A general view of a billboard featuring a Paddy Power advert that reads 'Shamchester', in Manchester, England, Wednesday, Sept. 30, 2026.
Manchester City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak, left, and chief executive Ferran Soriano arrive to watch the Champions League opening phase soccer match between Manchester City and Feyenoord at the Etihad Stadium in Manchester, England, Tuesday, Nov. 26, 2024.
FILE - Flares and tape are let off as Manchester City's players celebrate on stage as fans watch the winners parade as the team celebrates winning the English Premier League title in Manchester, England, Monday, May 23, 2022.
MANCHESTER, England (AP) — Manchester City fans are still processing Tuesday's landmark ruling that the most dominant Premier League team in recent times had, in fact, been found guilty of systematic financial breaches for nearly a decade to help boost its unprecedented era of success.
Kevin Parker, a fan for more than 50 years, has faith the club's Emirati ownership, which has turned City into a soccer powerhouse , will successfully clear its name.
“Everything that this ownership has said that they’re going to deliver, they delivered for me,” Parker told The Associated Press. “It would be the wrong time for me to suddenly lose faith.”
David Mooney, another longtime City fan, who runs popular podcasts about the club, describes himself as angry and conflicted. He is worried about what happens should the findings be upheld on appeal.
“This is probably setting the bar really low now, but whatever the outcome is, I just want City to still exist,” he said.
City was a storied club even before it was bought out by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, a member of the United Arab Emirates’ ruling family in 2008. It was one of the best supported teams in England, but had gone decades without winning a major trophy and lived in the shadow of its cross-city rival Manchester United.
The takeover transformed the landscape of the world’s most popular league with City going on to win eight titles, the Champions League and a slew of other trophies.
The possible sanctions for what amounts to the biggest scandal in Premier League history are wide ranging, up to and including expulsion from England's top flight .
An independent panel found City had set up complex schemes to disguise that it was unfairly being bankrolled by its owner , the Abu Dhabi United Group to the tune of more than $1 billion over a period of nine years from 2009-18. During that time it won three league titles, spent exorbitant sums to sign some of the best players in the world and appointed top-class coaches like Pep Guardiola.
In 2012 City was responsible for what is widely considered the most iconic Premier league moment when Sergio Aguero scored with virtually the last kick of the season to clinch the title from the then-dominant Man United.
A shadow now hangs over that achievement and many more following Tuesday's ruling, which City said it would appeal having consistently denied wrongdoing.
Some players, like United great Rio Ferdinand, have called for titles to be rescinded.
Defiant City fans have hit back at the very rules the club has been found in breach of.
“The biggest sham is that an owner putting his own money into his club to win titles is a crime,” prominent fan account PrestwichBlue posted on X.
There is, however, a sense of unease among some who were there for the moments of triumph over more than a decade of success that has now been called into question.
“It feels quite raw. I was there for the Aguero moment and I was there for the title in 2014 and the 100 points (title winning campaign in 2018),” said Mooney, who hosts the Bluemoon and Let Me Talk City podcasts. "I feel really sorry for the players because they had to still go out there and do it and achieve it."
But he accepts that because of the sheer amount of money that was found to have been pumped into the club “you can’t deny that there is a sporting advantage.”
A hearing into what sanctions should be placed on City is still to come. Potential punishments include huge fines and points deductions, as well as being booted out of the Premier League.
Mooney said there was a “sense that a lot of the football world wants blood.”
“At this stage the scale at which the verdict is guilty is damning and it’s huge. We’re way beyond slap-on-the-wrist territory here. But at the same time, we can’t have a punishment that effectively removes the club from from existence," he said.
The transformation since the takeover by Sheikh Mansour has not been limited to the team either, with huge investment going into the surrounding area including the construction of a state-of-the-art training academy, the biggest arena in the U.K. and a new hotel complex as well as the expansion of the soccer stadium.
“It’s unrecognizable that part of Manchester,” Parker said, pointing to the employment and money that has been generated as a result of the development driven by City's ownership. “All of those things are the things that make me think, why would they want to spoil that?”
In 2020 City successfully overturned a two-year ban from European competitions by UEFA for allegedly disguising funds, after appealing its case to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS).
Although an appeal on this occasion cannot go before CAS, Parker is confident City's ownership will prevail again because he says it has always delivered on its promises.
“Whether that be the case in CAS, or whether that be increasing the capacity of the stadium, whether that be signing the best players in the world, whether that be winning titles, winning the Champions League, bringing in the best coach in the world. They’ve never lied to us,” he said.

items.article_body:
SALA 2026, Day One: The annual South Asian Literature and Arts Festival (SALA) again drew an audience from far and wide. From almost the entire South Asian American community in California, anyone who could afford to walk, drive, ride, or fly to the venue had descended, like a flock of migrant birds, to the city of Atherton, where the festival was held September 26-27 on the grounds of Menlo College, unnoticed by students and faculty but much enjoyed by its regulars.
To some, it was a chance to see something new; for others, to reunite with old friends; to many, both. Also invited this year was the newly appointed Indian consul general in San Francisco, Satish Kumar Sivan.
The first act featured Kausar Munir, a lyricist and screenwriter for Yash Raj Films, Dharma Productions, Netflix, and Amazon, and the granddaughter of the renowned Urdu novelist Salma Siddiqui. Munir is also the first woman to win the Filmfare Award for Lyrics. She was introduced by the famous speaker and author Shikha Malaviya.
Before long, the auditorium was quite nearly a full house, and more than half the audience were paying attention, with the rule announced at the outset against personal video recording being broken only a dozen or so times.
The conversation proceeded at first along ordinary lines, with Munir saying she looks back on her previous creations either thinking her work might be better or being astounded at having written it so well, but prefers not to dwell on the past at all. When asked by Malaviya, “Where are you making a record? And where are you writing a love-letter?”, Munir gave no direct answer but explained her writing process, which seemed to serve that purpose admirably.
“It falls on a dialogue-writer… you have to make the plot… to be a bit of a performer,” said Munir. “There is no format… you have to feel your way through it”, and each collaboration between writer and director, she says, is different. Good directors are praised: “Amit Trivedi is… genuinely original… reacts very well to the script.”
“Do you have a favorite song you wrote?,” asked Malaviya. Munir replied, “Fun, party-songs are the most challenging to write, because you have no context.”
“Are lyrics poetry?” asked Malaviya, and Munir’s answer was essentially a ‘Yes’; but she places lyrics in a class by themselves, “because music and rhythm are important as words.”
“What does a poem mean to you, when you are writing a poem?,” asked Malaviya.
Munir replied, “This may sound Romantic;–– and I’m a fan of the Romantics! Shelley and Keats and Byron and all of them;–– it is a spontaneous expression of myself.”
Laughter and applause followed almost every remark, especially when Malaviya revealed, “The Internet thinks you’ve already written a book” (Munir protests she has no intention of writing one), “so we’re all waiting for it.”
When asked about the amalgam of languages in which her free verse is written, some of which she read aloud for the audience, Munir replied with the remark, worthy of passing into a proverb, “Jo zabaan bolté, Hindustani hé,” [“The language the people speak, is Hindustani].
Malaviya, author of Anandibai Joshee: A Life in Poems and co-founder of The (Great) Indian Poetry Collective, believes, “Everything women dream of, all they aspire to”; a recurring idea throughout various presentations all day.
In the next presentation, Dr. Venki Ramakrishnan, author of Why We Die, satisfies the audience’s need to learn from a Nobel laureate about ‘mortality’ and debunks the much-publicized efforts on the part of business magnates, after the fashion of powerful people since ancient times (his example is the Epic of Gilgamesh), to circumvent it.
In his lecture, Dr. Ramakrishnan makes comparisons across species, distinguishes life span from life expectancy, reminds us all of the basic premises of Natural Selection, and introduces the audience to the delicate balance every species must strike, with no two doing so identically, between the need of the individual for a long life and the need of the species for reproduction. Of interest to him is the idea of epigenetics, in which the most profound experiences of the individual may produce effects on its offspring, for example, the Dutch Famine and its effects on children born to those who suffered it.
Between such educational remarks, Dr. Ramakrishnan takes pains to dismiss what he calls “grand quackery”: namely, all popular claims about diets, fasts, cryonics, chemical treatments, and every other method of extending youth. “There are no long-term clinical trials,” he says, “and that’s what the science really needs.” His advice is simple: “Enjoy life; that’s going to make you live longer,” and, “Look at data carefully before spending money on supplements.”
Of disturbing interest to an anti-racist audience, Dr. Ramakrishnan informs us, “The same Body-Mass Index” may be normal in the European and excessive in the South Asian, African, or other diasporas, and this accounts for the latter appearing malnourished according to European or Euro-American measurements.
The last question came from a cryobiologist, who raised the possibility of using this technology for organ transplants; Dr. Ramakrishnan gently refuted this too.
At 3 p.m. in the Menlo College Student Union Building, the presentation on ‘Gaze from Nepal’ brought together the artists Tsherin Sherpa and Sneha Shrestha (better known as IMAGINE), both distinguished for combining ancient art with contemporary styles in pursuit of a new and global artistic ideal. Sherpa’s art has appeared at the Victoria & Albert Museum and the Asian Art Museum, and he himself appeared at the 2022 Venice Biennale, while IMAGINE’s art is the proud possession of the Harvard Art Museums and the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston. Moderator Padma Dorje brought them before a new viewing public, long accustomed to the work of artists and thinkers from other parts of the subcontinent, yet seldom privileged to see the rich heritage and cosmopolitan culture of modern-day Nepal.
Speaking first, Sherpa reminded the audience that traditional Nepali art is seen mostly in either religious or commercial settings, with nothing in between. He is the son of a traditional tankha artist, trained in the skills of his father from childhood, who set off early to make a name for himself as an artist of another kind, only to resume his ancestral art as the source of his own striking innovations: “to create”, he says, “a narrative… based on a more secular art… prayer flags” with a more human, even whimsical subject: one piece resembling a traditional prayer flag, but with advertising copy in the background disguised as prayer; a traditional Wrathful Deity design presented as a jumbled collage; another such design in an almost surrealist style; and a photograph of an abstract 3-dimensional installation.
Shrestha calls herself a lifelong artist, re-inspired by the idea of “letters as images” in street art in Boston, where she studied, and investigated Nepali traditions of calligraphy for its own sake: a form alive and well-known in the Arabic-writing world, but, IMAGINE says, deserving to be better known in Nepali Devanagari script. The audience was soon persuaded by examples of her work in a colorful slide show, from pages of translucent lettering in broad strokes on a solid-color background to brazen-colored panels of the Nepali kau, repeated, to the same in the form of a chandelier, to a mural six stories high, all meant, she said, to inspire still more such works in other artists. “At that point”, she says, “it belongs to the city, and that’s what I wanted.” Her sources, she says, vary from immigration forms to costumes worn by the artist’s elders.
IMAGINE concluded with a pavilion entitled ‘Why we Gather’ in Lo Manthang, Mustang, Nepal: a part of the world, she says, unused to rain; built to serve as a gathering hall for local people to discuss responses to the increasing rate of rainfall as a result of climate change. “To protect the living culture,” IMAGINE reminds us, “is also protecting the land.”
The next event, entitled ‘Desi Boys’, brought together Karan Mahajan, author of The Complex, and Aatish Taseer, author of Stranger to History, The Way Things Were, and The Temple-Goers, et al., moderated by Menlo College’s own Dr. Melissa Poulsen.
The two speakers are similar in appearance and manner, and played off one another’s speeches like a double act, each enlarging on the other’s remarks, talking along merrily like old friends, while the moderator, an example to moderators everywhere, kept both of them on the subject of their books and the status of Taseer as a political exile, his Overseas Citizenship of India recently revoked by the BJP government; to punish a satire, he says, of which he was the author, of Prime Minister Modi. “To lose one’s country is an intimate shame”, says Taseer. Mahajan adds, “OCI status can be taken away, but the Indian way of seeing the world cannot.”
Otherwise, Mahajan’s answers to most questions refer to his recent book, The Complex, which depicts the internal disagreements of a joint family in Delhi against the background of the larger internal disagreements of the Indian government shortly after Independence. Taseer contrasts longing for past glory with the American desire for “freedom” from the past; Mahajan adds, “All wish to be loved and understood… also a form of longing,” or of grievance.
In conclusion, the two speakers laugh at the presentation’s title of ‘Desi Boys’; Mahajan adds, referring to Taseer, “Pakistani Boy… but that’s Desi too.”
Final remarks ranged far and wide, especially on the part of Taseer, who claims to have known the last of the literary Schoenberg family, themselves friends of the great German writer Thomas Mann: exiles, like himself, with the subject and style of their writings forever altered and defined, as an audience question implied, by that exile.
Racism was also discussed. Taseer cites Shakespeare’s Tragedy of Othello and explains its antagonist ‘Iago’ as “an untalented mediocrity jealous of a talented outsider”; an archetype to explain, not Mahajan’s “Laxman Chopra” character alone, but nationalists and ethno-nationalists everywhere.
“Are the populations [within a nation] mixing?”, asks Mahajan, suggesting they are subject to discrimination and being forced out if not. Integration and assimilation were discussed at length by Mahajan, to the laughter and agreement, as with most of his remarks, of the audience. Taseer, meanwhile, informs us, In Buddhism, longing for the past, or for a lost home is a form of attachment, to be overcome by the disciplined seeker.
Shobhaa De, the last speaker for Day One, is the author of the largest number of books, and also the lightest reading; for her books depict neither the misfortunes of the Everyman nor the harrowing events of our century, but her own emotions, principally pleasures. Thus, she is the most fashionable of this year’s authors and offers a relief from the tragedies of the times, as well as a counterweight to the ascetic traditions of which the Indian diaspora is justly proud. “Indian culture”, according to De, is built for delight in food, clothes, music, and affection. This year, she was introduced and interviewed by Dr. Anjali Arondekar, another SALA regular.
“For me,” says De, “the voice is everything; I have to find it,” in every book she writes, of which there are now 28; “across genres”, says Arondekar. In this, she represents an exception to the usual rule, cited by Dr. Ramakrishnan today, that writers’ and artists’ imaginations decline after their middle years.
Like love poetry or erotic sculpture, De’s books remind us that the austerity of the spiritual and the delights of the sensual life can exist in the same tradition, time, and culture without endangering one another. “We have,” De says, “in a way, undermined and under-rated it [Sensuality]”; the rising generation is lost for words about eating, drinking, seeking a lover, and ot
items.title_zh: 南亚多元声音汇聚：从Kausar Munir到Venki Ramakrishnan
items.summary_zh: 本文探讨了南亚科学家在延长青春的饮食和冷冻技术等领域的观点，指出这些流行方法缺乏长期临床试验的支持。科学家们强调，科学研究需要更多的数据来验证这些方法的有效性。Kausar Munir提到：“没有长期临床试验，这正是科学所需。”而Venki Ramakrishnan则建议人们享受生活，以此来延长寿命。此外，科学家们还提醒消费者在购买补充剂前要仔细查看数据。这些观点共同指向了对科学研究和数据支持的迫切需求。
items.l1_lead: 南亚科学家呼吁对延长青春的饮食和冷冻技术进行更多长期临床试验，以验证其有效性，并提醒消费者关注数据支持。
items.l2_summary:
本文探讨了南亚科学家在延长青春的饮食和冷冻技术等领域的观点，强调这些流行方法缺乏长期临床试验的支持，亟需更多的数据来验证其有效性。Kausar Munir指出：“没有长期临床试验，这正是科学所需。”这一观点反映了科学界对数据支持的迫切需求，尤其是在涉及健康和寿命延长的领域。与此同时，诺贝尔奖得主Venki Ramakrishnan则提出了另一种生活态度，他建议人们应享受生活，以此来延长寿命。这一建议虽然与科学研究的严谨性有所不同，但也强调了生活质量的重要性。

科学家们还提醒消费者在购买补充剂时要仔细查看相关数据，以确保所选产品的安全性和有效性。这一警示进一步突显了科学研究在健康领域的重要性，尤其是在面对市场上众多未经验证的产品时。总的来说，南亚科学家们的观点共同指向了对科学研究和数据支持的迫切需求，呼吁在健康和营养领域的创新应建立在扎实的科学基础之上。

items.title: How to Be a More Hopeful Neighbor: Be a Better Colleague（41:30）
items.body:
原话（41:30）：“I would say at the heart of some of these issues is individualism and an individualistic understanding of vocation calling occupation profession.”
论点：个体主义的理解阻碍了团队合作和共同使命感。
论据：我们可以非常个体化地思考，而缺乏对共同体的欣赏，这是一个问题。

items.title_zh: 如何成为更好的同事：个体主义的影响
items.summary_zh: 本文探讨了个体主义对团队合作和共同使命感的影响。作者指出，个体主义的理解阻碍了人们对职业（vocation）和工作的共同体意识，导致在思考时过于关注个人而忽视集体的价值。个体化的思维方式使得人们缺乏对共同体的欣赏，这一问题在团队协作中尤为明显。通过强调集体意识的重要性，文章呼吁人们在职业生涯中更好地融入团队，以促进合作与共同目标的实现。
items.l1_lead: 个体主义妨碍了团队合作与共同使命感，强调集体意识对职业生涯和团队协作的重要性。
items.l2_summary:
本文探讨了个体主义（individualism）对团队合作和共同使命感的影响，指出个体主义的理解在一定程度上阻碍了人们对职业（vocation）和工作的共同体意识。这种思维方式使得个体在思考时过于关注个人利益，而忽视了集体的价值和目标，导致团队协作中的问题愈加明显。个体化的思维方式使得人们缺乏对共同体的欣赏，进而影响了团队的凝聚力和合作效率。

文章强调，集体意识的重要性不可忽视，尤其是在现代职场中，团队的成功往往依赖于成员之间的协作与共同努力。通过增强集体意识，个体能够更好地融入团队，促进合作与共同目标的实现。作者呼吁人们在职业生涯中，尤其是在团队环境中，积极培养和维护共同体意识，以提升整体工作效率和团队表现。

总的来说，个体主义的盛行可能导致团队成员之间的隔阂，影响集体的协作精神。因此，重视集体意识，增强团队合作能力，将有助于在职业发展中实现更大的成功。

items.title: How to Be a More Hopeful Neighbor: Be a Better Colleague（44:56）
items.body:
原话（44:56）：“If you do the right thing. If you do the if you do things well, the reward is greater than your reputation.”
论点：做好工作比追求声誉更重要，真正的回报在于工作的质量。
论据：如果你做得好，回报会超过你的声誉。

items.claim_zh: 做好工作比追求声誉更重要，真正的回报在于工作的质量。
items.evidence_zh: 如果你做得好，回报会超过你的声誉。
items.title_zh: 如何成为更好的同事：重视工作质量
items.summary_zh: 本文探讨了在职场中，做好工作的重要性，强调工作质量比追求声誉更为关键。作者指出，如果你能够认真做好自己的工作，所获得的回报将会超越个人声誉。这一观点提醒我们，真正的成就来自于对工作的投入与执行，而非外界的评价。通过强调工作质量的重要性，文章鼓励职场人士专注于自身的职业表现，以实现更高的职业回报。
items.l1_lead: 重视工作质量比追求声誉更为关键，真正的成就源于对工作的投入与执行。
items.l2_summary:
在职场中，工作质量的重要性不容忽视。本文探讨了如何成为更好的同事，强调了重视工作质量比追求个人声誉更为关键。作者指出，认真做好自己的工作所获得的回报往往会超越个人的声誉。这一观点提醒我们，真正的成就源于对工作的投入与执行，而非外界的评价。通过专注于自身的职业表现，职场人士能够实现更高的职业回报。

在现代职场环境中，许多人往往过于关注外界对自己的评价，试图通过建立声誉来获得认可。然而，作者强调，声誉的建立是建立在实际工作表现之上的，只有通过高质量的工作，才能赢得同事和上司的尊重与信任。工作质量不仅体现在完成任务的效率上，更体现在对工作的认真态度和对细节的关注。高质量的工作能够提升团队的整体表现，进而推动个人职业发展的良性循环。

此外，文章还提到，职场人士应当将重心放在提升自身技能和专业素养上，而不是单纯追求外在的认可。通过不断学习和实践，提升工作质量，最终将会在职业生涯中获得更丰厚的回报。作者的论点强调了在职场中，真正的成功来自于对工作的热情与投入，而非对声誉的盲目追求。

总之，重视工作质量是成为更好同事的关键。通过专注于自身的职业表现，职场人士不仅能够提升个人能力，还能为团队和组织创造更大的价值。最终，真正的成就将会在于对工作的认真态度和高质量的执行，而非外界的评价和声誉。

items.title: How to Be a More Hopeful Neighbor: Be a Better Colleague（28:50）
items.body:
原话（28:50）：“the conflict is profession professional the professional and the personal.”
论点：在职业和个人生活中，专业与个人之间存在冲突。
论据：这段转写中提到，节目揭示了职业与个人之间的冲突，强调了在工作环境中如何平衡这两者。

items.title_zh: 如何成为更好的同事：职业与个人的冲突
items.summary_zh: 本文探讨了在职业生活中，专业与个人之间的冲突。作者指出，这种冲突在工作环境中尤为明显，影响着同事之间的关系和工作效率。通过节目中的讨论，强调了平衡职业责任与个人生活的重要性，建议同事们在面对这种冲突时，采取更为积极的态度，以促进更好的合作与沟通。最终，文章呼吁关注这一问题，以提升工作环境的和谐性和生产力。
items.l1_lead: 平衡职业责任与个人生活对于改善同事关系和提升工作效率至关重要，积极应对冲突有助于促进合作与沟通。
items.l2_summary:
在现代职场中，职业责任与个人生活之间的冲突日益显著，这一问题对同事之间的关系和工作效率产生了深远的影响。本文深入探讨了这一现象，强调了在工作环境中平衡专业与个人生活的重要性。作者通过节目讨论，指出许多员工在面对工作压力时，常常感到难以兼顾家庭、健康和个人兴趣等方面的需求，这种冲突不仅影响了他们的心理健康，也降低了工作效率。

为了解决这一问题，作者建议同事们应采取更为积极的态度，主动寻求平衡。具体而言，团队成员可以通过开放的沟通和相互理解来缓解职业与个人生活之间的紧张关系。例如，定期的团队会议可以为员工提供一个分享个人需求和职业挑战的平台，从而促进彼此之间的理解与支持。此外，企业也应当关注员工的个人生活，提供灵活的工作安排和心理健康支持，以帮助员工更好地应对生活中的各种挑战。

文章最后呼吁，关注职业与个人冲突的问题不仅有助于提升工作环境的和谐性，还能显著提高整体生产力。通过建立一个更加包容和理解的工作氛围，企业和员工都能在各自的角色中获得更大的满足感与成就感，从而实现个人与职业的双赢。

items.title_zh: Tirzepatide对糖尿病患者心血管保护的影响
items.summary_zh: 本文讨论了Tirzepatide（Tisepathy）在糖尿病患者中的应用，强调其对心血管疾病的保护作用。科学家Naveed Sattar指出，Tirzepatide为糖尿病患者提供了心血管保护的信心，帮助他们更好地应对糖尿病与心血管疾病共存的挑战。关键证据是美国食品药品监督管理局（FDA）已批准Tirzepatide作为糖尿病患者的心血管保护药物。这一批准为临床实践提供了重要支持，表明Tirzepatide在改善糖尿病患者的整体健康状况方面具有潜力。
items.l1_lead: Tirzepatide被FDA批准用于糖尿病患者，显示出其在心血管保护方面的潜力，为患者应对糖尿病与心血管疾病的共存提供了信心。
items.l2_summary:
Tirzepatide（Tisepathy）是一种新型药物，近年来在糖尿病患者中的应用引起了广泛关注，尤其是在其对心血管疾病的保护作用方面。科学家Naveed Sattar指出，Tirzepatide为糖尿病患者提供了心血管保护的信心，帮助他们更有效地应对糖尿病与心血管疾病共存的挑战。值得注意的是，美国食品药品监督管理局（FDA）已批准Tirzepatide作为糖尿病患者的心血管保护药物，这一批准为临床实践提供了重要支持，表明Tirzepatide在改善糖尿病患者的整体健康状况方面具有显著潜力。

这一研究强调了Tirzepatide在心血管保护方面的关键作用，尤其是在糖尿病患者中，心血管疾病的风险普遍较高。通过临床试验和研究数据，Tirzepatide被证明能够有效降低心血管事件的发生率，从而为糖尿病患者的心血管健康提供了新的治疗选择。这一发现不仅为患者带来了希望，也为医生在治疗糖尿病患者时提供了新的思路和方法。

总的来说，Tirzepatide的批准和应用标志着糖尿病治疗领域的一次重要进展，尤其是在心血管保护方面的潜力，能够帮助患者更好地管理他们的健康状况，降低心血管疾病的风险。这一研究成果为未来的临床实践奠定了基础，推动了糖尿病与心血管疾病的综合管理策略的发展。

items.title_zh: Tirzepatide降低心血管事件，C-Peptide对T1D进展的见解
items.summary_zh: 本文讨论了Tirzepatide在降低心血管事件方面的效果，以及C-Peptide在1型糖尿病（T1D）进展中的作用。研究表明，Tirzepatide相比安慰剂确实降低了心血管事件的发生率，多个分析方法的结果均显示出显著的心血管风险降低。此外，Emily Sims的研究提供了C-Peptide在糖尿病进展过程中的重要见解，强调了其在监测和理解T1D进展中的潜在价值。这些发现为临床实践提供了新的视角，可能影响未来的治疗策略。
items.l1_lead: Tirzepatide显著降低心血管事件发生率，同时C-Peptide在1型糖尿病进展中提供了重要见解，可能影响未来的治疗策略。
items.l2_summary:
本文探讨了Tirzepatide在降低心血管事件方面的效果，以及C-Peptide（C肽）在1型糖尿病（T1D）进展中的作用。研究结果表明，Tirzepatide相较于安慰剂显著降低了心血管事件的发生率，多个分析方法的结果均显示出心血管风险的显著降低。这一发现为临床实践提供了新的视角，可能会影响未来的治疗策略。

此外，Emily Sims的研究为C-Peptide在糖尿病进展过程中的重要性提供了深入见解。C-Peptide作为胰岛素分泌的标志物，其水平的变化能够反映胰腺β细胞的功能状态，从而为监测和理解T1D的进展提供了潜在的价值。通过对C-Peptide的研究，能够更好地评估T1D患者的病情变化，进而为个体化治疗方案的制定提供依据。

综上所述，Tirzepatide在心血管事件预防方面的积极效果，以及C-Peptide在T1D进展监测中的重要作用，均为糖尿病及其并发症的治疗提供了新的思路和方向。这些研究成果不仅丰富了我们对糖尿病病理生理的理解，也为临床医生在制定治疗方案时提供了重要的参考依据。

items.body:
原话：“complications can build up over time as high blood sugar, high blood pressure, unhealthy blood fat levels and obesity damage blood vessels and vital organs.” / “the importance of detecting and treating type 2 diabetes as early and comprehensively as possible.”
论点：高血糖、高血压、不健康的血脂水平和肥胖会导致肾脏疾病在心力衰竭之前出现。
论据：在五年内，19.0%的患者首先发展为慢性肾脏疾病，而8.3%的患者首先发展为心力衰竭。

items.topic_zh: 糖尿病与肾脏疾病和心力衰竭的关系
items.claim_zh: 高血糖、高血压、不健康的血脂水平和肥胖会导致肾脏疾病在心力衰竭之前出现。
items.evidence_zh: 在五年内，19.0%的患者首先发展为慢性肾脏疾病，而8.3%的患者首先发展为心力衰竭。
items.article_body:
Kidney disease can develop before heart failure in people newly diagnosed with type 2 diabetes, according to new research reported by Knowridge. The study analysed data from nearly 1.62 million adults.
The findings were presented at the annual meeting of the European Association for the Study of Diabetes, held in Milan from 28 September to 2 October. The study was led by Dr Naveed Sattar of the University of Glasgow in the UK.
The researchers examined which complication occurred first after a diagnosis of type 2 diabetes. Within five years, 19.0 per cent of patients had developed chronic kidney disease first, compared with 8.3 per cent who developed heart failure first.
The relationship between the two organs was found to work in both directions. Among people with chronic kidney disease, 22.7 per cent developed heart failure within five years. Among those with heart failure, 42.0 per cent developed chronic kidney disease over the following five years.
When chronic kidney disease, heart failure and death were considered together, the risk was 32.9 per cent within five years of a type 2 diabetes diagnosis. After 10 years, it had risen to 55.1 per cent.
Chronic kidney disease means that the kidneys gradually lose their ability to filter waste products and excess fluid from the blood. In its early stages, it can cause few noticeable symptoms, making blood and urine tests important for detecting it.
According to Sattar, complications can build up over time as high blood sugar, high blood pressure, unhealthy blood fat levels and obesity damage blood vessels and vital organs. He stressed the importance of detecting and treating type 2 diabetes as early and comprehensively as possible.
The findings describe risk across a large population and cannot predict what will happen to an individual. They were presented at a scientific meeting, so the full published study and the methods used in the research should also be taken into account when assessing the evidence. | BGNES
items.title_zh: 研究发现2型糖尿病患者肾病早于心力衰竭出现
items.summary_zh: 一项研究指出，在2型糖尿病患者中，高血糖、高血压、不健康的血脂水平和肥胖等因素会导致肾脏疾病在心力衰竭之前出现。研究数据显示，在五年内，19.0%的患者首先发展为慢性肾脏疾病，而8.3%的患者则首先发展为心力衰竭。这一发现强调了尽早、全面检测和治疗2型糖尿病的重要性，以减少并发症的发生。
items.l1_lead: 研究表明，2型糖尿病患者中，肾病的发生往往早于心力衰竭，强调了早期检测和治疗的重要性。
items.l2_summary: 一项针对2型糖尿病患者的研究发现，肾脏疾病的发生往往早于心力衰竭（heart failure）。研究指出，高血糖、高血压、不健康的血脂水平以及肥胖等因素是导致这一现象的主要原因。在观察的五年内，19.0%的患者首先发展为慢性肾脏疾病（chronic kidney disease），而只有8.3%的患者首先发展为心力衰竭。这一数据表明，肾脏疾病在2型糖尿病患者中更为常见且更早出现，提示临床医生在管理糖尿病患者时，应更加关注肾脏健康。研究结果强调了对2型糖尿病患者进行早期、全面的检测和治疗的重要性，以减少肾脏疾病及其他并发症的发生。这一发现不仅为临床实践提供了重要的参考依据，也为未来的研究方向指明了道路，促使医疗界更加重视糖尿病患者的肾脏健康管理。

items.body:
原话：“Patients and physicians need therapies that sustain metabolic benefit over time.” / “ENV-308 represents a novel approach targeting this challenge, and it is encouraging to see early clinical data from a new mechanism of action supporting its progression into later-stage clinical trials.”

items.claim_zh: ENV-308是一种新型药物，能够在减肥治疗中提供持续的代谢益处。
items.evidence_zh: 早期临床数据支持其进入后期临床试验。
items.article_body:
See more of our coverage in your search results.
Gym haters, rejoice — the workout of the future may not require breaking a sweat.
Biotech company Enveda announced this week that its experimental drug, designed to curb appetite and mimic some of the body’s effects of physical activity, delivered encouraging results in its first clinical trial.
“ENV-308 is our attempt to put the chemistry of exercise into a daily tablet,” Viswa Colluru, the startup’s founder and CEO, said in a statement .
The early results are drawing attention because the new drug could offer a GLP-1-like approach to weight loss — without some of the class’s biggest drawbacks, including gastrointestinal side effects and muscle loss.
The pill mimics a molecule called lactate phenylalanine, or Lac-Phe, which scientists at Stanford discovered in 2022.
The body produces it naturally when lactate — a chemical released by muscles during vigorous exercise — combines with the amino acid phenylalanine.
Once it enters the bloodstream, Lac-Phe acts sends a signal to the brain to dial down the drive to eat. Studies in animals have also found that it can suppress appetite and reduce obesity.
There’s just one catch: Lac-Phe breaks down quickly, so it doesn’t stay in the bloodstream long enough to keep the urge to eat at bay throughout the day and promote lasting weight loss.
That’s where ENV-308 comes in. Enveda’s pill aims to harness Lac-Phe’s benefits in a daily oral tablet, potentially making them last longer.
In a Phase 1 clinical trial, Enveda gave ENV-308 at varying strengths to 88 healthy adults. Notably, the experiment didn’t set out to determine whether the drug actually helped with weight loss. Instead, researchers were primarily looking at whether it was safe.
They found that the participants tolerated the drug across the full range of doses tested, with the company reporting it had an “exceptional gastrointestinal safety profile.”
That could be a big deal in the weight-loss-drug world.
Nausea, vomiting and other gastrointestinal problems are among the most common reasons people stop taking GLP-1s , the blockbuster class of medications that includes medications such as Ozempic and Wegovy.
In animal studies, ENV-308 also preserved lean muscle mass during weight loss. That’s significant because research suggests that some of the pounds people lose while taking GLP-1s can come from muscle , not just fat.
Animals also maintained their slimmer figures after scientists stopped giving them ENV-308. That could be particularly important, since many people who stop taking GLP-1 drugs regain some of the weight they lost — and sometimes even more.
“Patients and physicians need therapies that sustain metabolic benefit over time,” said Dr. Naveed Sattar, a professor of metabolic medicine at the University of Glasgow and chair of the UK’s Obesity Healthcare Goals Program.
“ENV-308 represents a novel approach targeting this challenge, and it is encouraging to see early clinical data from a new mechanism of action supporting its progression into later-stage clinical trials.”
Still, don’t expect ENV-308 to send Ozempic packing just yet.
Enveda says the pill could potentially be used alongside existing therapies like GLP-1s, including possibly allowing them to be taken less frequently. The company is also exploring whether the approach could help avoid some of the side effects associated with the treatments .
The Phase I trial also looked at leptin, a hormone that helps regulate hunger. People with obesity often have high leptin levels but can become resistant to its signals.
Early results suggest that ENV-308 lowers leptin levels in animals and humans, with the biggest drops seen in participants who started with the highest levels.
“There is now compelling data in preclinical models indicating that Lac-Phe is involved in regulating several aspects of metabolic, brain, and inflammatory health,” said Dr. Jonathan Long, a leading researcher in exercise metabolism and advisor to Enveda.
“The possibility that ENV-308 may mimic these effects in a daily oral tablet in humans is an extremely exciting potential scientific breakthrough.”
In the next round of trials, researchers will look at whether ENV-308 can actually affect body weight and composition, as well as leptin biology and other markers of metabolic health. They’ll also study how the drug interacts with GLP-1 medications.
But Enveda isn’t stopping at weight loss.
The company also plans to study whether ENV-308 could help treat other conditions where exercise may be beneficial, including migraines , inflammatory bowel disease and polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome , formerly known as polycystic ovary syndrome.
But don’t expect to get a prescription anytime soon. ENV-308 is still in the early stages of development, and it will take years to determine whether it works and is safe for long-term use.
Even if those trials succeed, the pill would still need approval from the Food and Drug Administration before it could become available to the public.
If it does reach the market, don’t cancel your gym membership just yet. While ENV-308 aims to mimic some of the effects of exercise, working out does a lot more than burn calories.
Physical activity can improve mental health , support brain function , promote better sleep , boost energy, reduce inflammation, strengthen the immune system and support a healthy gut — benefits you’ll still need to break a sweat to get.

items.title: Swiss unions want a 2% pay rise. Employers are unconvinced - Le News
items.body:
原话：“household finances have deteriorated as wages have failed to keep pace with the cost of living.”
论点：家庭财务状况恶化，因为工资未能跟上生活成本的增长。
论据：在2022年至2026年末之间，中等收入家庭的购买力预计将下降1.5-1.9%。
items.attribution_basis: Google News 全名命中 + LLM 同一人核验（Le News） + 论点方向独立复核
quotes: household finances have deteriorated as wages have failed to keep pace with the cost of living.
items.claim_zh: 家庭财务状况恶化，因为工资未能跟上生活成本的增长。
items.evidence_zh: 在2022年至2026年末之间，中等收入家庭的购买力预计将下降1.5-1.9%。
items.article_body:
With inflation running at just 0.4%, the battle over wages in 2027 may be as much about productivity growth as lost purchasing power. In any case Switzerland’s wage negotiations for 2027 are shaping up to be contentious.
Travail.Suisse, a trade-union federation, is demanding an across-the-board pay rise of 2% . The Swiss Employers’ Association, by contrast, reckons an average increase of around 1% would be more realistic.
The unions’ demand is an average and varies considerably by industry. In healthcare, Syna, one of Travail.Suisse’s member unions, is calling for increases of 5-6%, arguing that modest wage settlements in recent years have badly eroded workers’ purchasing power.
Travail.Suisse’s case rests less on today’s inflation than on what it sees as a decade of disappointing real-wage growth. Thomas Bauer, the federation’s head of economic policy, argues that household finances have deteriorated as wages have failed to keep pace with the cost of living.
Health-insurance premiums are a particular sore point. They are not included in Switzerland’s consumer-price index and have risen sharply in recent years. Travail.Suisse estimates that, once higher premiums and inflation are taken into account, the purchasing power of middle-income households will have fallen by 1.5-1.9% between 2022 and the end of 2026.
The unions also complain of a widening gap between wages and productivity. Labour productivity, they say, increased by an average of 1.4% a year between 2017 and 2026, without a corresponding rise in real wages. In their telling, the gains have flowed disproportionately to capital rather than labour.
Employers reject both the diagnosis and the prescription . The Swiss Employers’ Association says a 2% rise ignores weak economic growth and geopolitical uncertainty, and argues that protecting jobs should take priority. It also disputes the unions’ claim that companies have pocketed productivity gains.
At the heart of the disagreement is a statistical argument. Employers say unions rely too heavily on the Swiss wage index, which does not fully capture promotions or workers moving into better-paid jobs. Using total employee compensation per hour worked, they argue, real pay has risen at least as fast as productivity since 2014.
Both sides agree on one thing: rising health-insurance premiums are squeezing households. But they draw different conclusions. Employers point out that in 2025 disposable income increased by CHF 48 per person per month, while higher net premiums absorbed CHF 12, leaving households CHF 36 better off. For unions, the pressure from insurance bills strengthens the case for bigger pay rises. Employers say the answer lies instead in restraining healthcare costs.
The timing makes the unions’ demand harder to sell. Consumer prices fell by 0.1% in July, while annual inflation stood at just 0.4%. A 2% wage increase would therefore amount to a sizeable real-terms rise if inflation remains this subdued. Travail.Suisse will argue that workers are owed compensation for past losses and productivity gains; employers will counter that wage settlements should reflect the economy they expect in 2027.
For more stories like this on Switzerland follow us on Facebook and X .

items.title_zh: 运动如何减缓衰老的科学探讨
items.summary_zh: 本文探讨了运动对衰老的影响，核心论点是运动是一种强效的药物，但其剂量至关重要。研究表明，适量的运动能够带来长寿的益处，但过量运动可能会削弱这些益处，甚至产生负面效果。因此，科学合理地安排运动量是保持健康和延缓衰老的关键。

items.l2_summary:
本文探讨了运动对衰老的影响，强调运动作为一种强效的药物，其剂量的合理安排至关重要。研究表明，适量的运动能够显著延长寿命，带来多种健康益处。然而，过量运动则可能削弱这些益处，甚至导致负面效果。因此，科学合理地安排运动量是保持健康和延缓衰老的关键。

在研究中，适度运动被定义为每周150分钟的中等强度运动，这一标准被广泛认可并支持了长寿的相关性。相反，过量运动，尤其是高强度的训练，可能会导致身体的过度疲劳和免疫系统的抑制，进而影响健康。研究还指出，适度运动不仅能改善心血管健康，还能增强肌肉力量和灵活性，降低慢性疾病的风险。

此外，运动对心理健康的积极影响也不容忽视。适量的运动能够释放内啡肽，改善情绪，减轻焦虑和抑郁症状，从而提升整体生活质量。综上所述，运动在延缓衰老方面的作用是显而易见的，但关键在于找到适合自己的运动量，以确保其带来的健康益处最大化。

本文探讨了运动对衰老过程的影响，强调了现代生活方式与人类生物学之间的不匹配问题，提出解决这一问题的关键在于恢复我们的生物本能，而非与之对抗。科学家们指出，保持健康和功能的关键在于重新激活进化过程中形成的运动系统。研究表明，适当的运动不仅能够延缓衰老，还能促进整体健康，强调了生物学与生活方式之间的和谐关系。

运动被认为是对抗衰老的重要手段，通过激活体内的生物机制，帮助维持身体的健康状态。科学家们的研究表明，规律的身体活动能够改善心血管健康、增强肌肉力量、提高代谢率，并且有助于维持认知功能。这些生理变化不仅有助于延缓衰老的过程，还能显著提高生活质量。运动的益处在于其能够促进身体的自我修复能力，增强免疫系统，降低慢性疾病的风险。

此外，运动还被发现能够影响基因表达，激活与衰老相关的生物通路，从而在分子层面上减缓衰老过程。研究显示，参与定期运动的人群，其生物年龄（biological age）往往低于其实际年龄（chronological age），这表明运动在生物学层面上具有显著的抗衰老效果。

综上所述，运动不仅是延缓衰老的有效手段，更是促进整体健康的重要因素。通过恢复与进化相适应的运动习惯，我们可以更好地应对现代生活带来的挑战，提升生活质量，延长健康寿命。因此，科学家们呼吁人们重视运动在日常生活中的重要性，以实现生物学与生活方式的和谐统一。

items.title: PCN-700: A Model Platform for Crystallographic Probing of Coordination Behavior in Metal-Organic Frameworks.
items.body: Coordination chemistry plays pivotal roles across a broad range of chemical, biological, and materials fields. Crystalline coordination materials provide unique opportunities for investigating coordination phenomena because their long-range structural order enables atomic-resolution characterization of coordination environments and structure-property relationships. Among them, metal-organic frameworks have greatly expanded the scope of coordination chemistry through their highly tunable compositions and spatial arrangements. To simplify the complexity associated with framework construction, post-synthetic modification has emerged as an effective strategy for systematically tailoring existing frameworks while preserving their networks. Nevertheless, conventional modification approaches remain limited in installation efficiency and coordination investigation. The discovery of PCN-700 together with the linker installation strategy has largely overcome these limitations. Owing to its highly uncoordinated zirconium clusters, predefined installation sites, and exceptional framework flexibility, PCN-700 enables efficient installation while maintaining crystallinity, allowing atomic-resolution visualization. Besides, linker installation decouples coordination from crystallization, transforming framework construction into controllable events at predefined crystallographic sites. In this review, we discuss linker installation pathways, host-guest interactions, and structure-enabled applications in PCN-700, highlighting the role of linker installation in establishing PCN-700 as a model system for elucidating fundamental coordination chemistry, quantitatively correlating coordination events with material properties, and guiding the rational design of functional materials.
items.authors: Han Z, Huo J, Zhou HC.
items.title_zh: PCN-700：金属有机框架中配位行为的晶体探测模型平台
items.summary_zh: 配位化学在化学、生物和材料领域中发挥着关键作用。晶体配位材料因其长程结构有序性，提供了以原子分辨率表征配位环境和结构-性质关系的独特机会。金属有机框架（MOFs）通过其高度可调的组成和空间排列，极大地扩展了配位化学的范围。后合成修饰作为一种有效策略，能够在保持框架网络的同时系统性地调整现有框架。然而，传统的修饰方法在安装效率和配位研究方面仍然有限。PCN-700的发现及其连接体安装策略在很大程度上克服了这些限制。得益于其高度不配位的锆簇、预定义的安装位点和卓越的框架灵活性，PCN-700实现了高效安装并保持晶体性，允许原子分辨率的可视化。此外，连接体安装将配位与结晶解耦，将框架构建转变为在预定义晶体学位点上的可控事件。
items.l1_lead: PCN-700通过其独特的结构和连接体安装策略，显著提升了金属有机框架中配位化学的研究效率，实现了高效安装和原子分辨率的可视化。
items.l2_summary:
配位化学在化学、生物和材料科学中具有重要的作用，而晶体配位材料因其长程结构的有序性，提供了以原子分辨率表征配位环境和结构-性质关系的独特机会。金属有机框架（MOFs）因其高度可调的组成和空间排列，极大地扩展了配位化学的应用范围。后合成修饰作为一种有效的策略，能够在保持框架网络的同时系统性地调整现有框架。然而，传统的修饰方法在安装效率和配位研究方面存在一定的局限性。

PCN-700的发现及其连接体安装策略在很大程度上克服了这些限制。PCN-700的结构特点包括高度不配位的锆簇、预定义的安装位点以及卓越的框架灵活性，这些特性使得其能够实现高效的连接体安装，同时保持晶体的完整性。这一过程允许研究者以原子分辨率对配位环境进行可视化。此外，连接体的安装将配位与结晶解耦，转变为在预定义晶体学位点上的可控事件，从而为配位化学的研究提供了新的思路和方法。

通过PCN-700的研究，科学家们能够更深入地理解配位化学的基本原理，并为未来的材料设计和功能化提供了新的平台。这一成果不仅推动了金属有机框架的研究进展，也为相关领域的科学探索开辟了新的方向。

Published: 18:01 EDT, 26 September 2026 | Updated: 18:25 EDT, 26 September 2026
Up to a third of people with type 2 diabetes will develop heart failure, kidney disease or die within five years of their diagnosis, a major study has found.
Over ten years, this risk increases to more than 55 per cent.
Researchers from the University of Glasgow say the findings highlight the importance of catching the condition early, and making lifestyle changes to reduce the risk of serious complications.
Almost 4.2 million people in the UK have been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes, while a further 1.3 million are estimated to be living with the disease without a diagnosis.
The condition is a leading cause of blindness, kidney failure, heart attack, and stroke and occurs when the body does not respond properly to – or make enough – insulin, causing blood sugar to rise dangerously high.
It is often linked to obesity and fuelled by poor diets, with rates having surged by almost 70 per cent among young women in England over the last decade.
'Our findings clearly show how the serious complications associated with type 2 diabetes rise sharply over time as obesity, abnormal blood fats, high blood pressure and high blood sugar damage blood vessels and vital organs,' said Professor Naveed Sattar, the study's lead author.
'Our results emphasise the critical importance of detecting and treating type 2 diabetes thoroughly at the earliest opportunity to help reduce the risk of serious complications.'
Up to a third of people with type 2 diabetes will develop heart failure, kidney disease or die within five years of diagnosis
The study – which is being presented at the Annual Meeting of the European Association for the Study of Diabetes – analysed data from more than 1.6 million Americans diagnosed with the disease between January 2010 and March 2024.
The average age of participants was 59 and among the patients who had a body mass index recorded, the average was 31 – placing them in the obese category.
Almost three-quarters of participants also had high cholesterol and more than two thirds had high blood pressure.
Researchers found that within five years of a diagnosis, nearly one in five patients developed chronic kidney disease – a condition in which the kidneys gradually lose the ability to filter waste from the blood.
This was more than double the risk of heart failure – where the heart can no longer pump blood effectively around the body.
However, those who developed heart failure first faced a 42 per cent increased risk of developing chronic kidney disease within the next five years.
Meanwhile, those who developed kidney damage first were 23 per cent more likely to develop heart failure over the same period.
Taken together, the findings suggest that damage to the heart and kidneys may accelerate damage to other organs, creating a vicious cycle of declining health.
Because the study was observational, the researchers stressed it cannot prove cause and effect.
The head of clinical at Diabetes UK added: 'Heart failure and kidney disease are serious complications of type 2 diabetes, but they are not inevitable.
'This research is an important reminder of the value of understanding your risk of developing type 2 diabetes, getting an early diagnosis and access to the right care and treatment.'
The findings add to growing evidence that the impact of type 2 diabetes extends far beyond blood sugar control alone.
It comes following a series of studies linking type 2 diabetes with a number of deadly cancers, including breast, bowel and lung.
Another study presented at the conference found women with the condition face a 22 per cent higher risk of cancer than those without, while men are 12 per cent more likely to develop the disease.
The risk is most pronounced for obesity-related cancers, including kidney, pancreatic and liver.
Previous research suggests cancer is now the leading cause of death among those with type 2 diabetes in Britain.
But with an estimated nine in ten cases linked to excess weight, experts believe weight loss jabs like Wegovy and Mounjaro could help turn the tide on the diabetes epidemic.
The drugs – originally developed to treat diabetes – are now used to help people lose excess weight, manage blood sugar, and prevent heart attacks.
Research has also suggested they can cut the risk of kidney disease by 24 per cent.
Chronic kidney disease is estimated to affect one in ten people worldwide, equivalent to about 850 million people. It is projected to become the fifth most common cause of death by 2050.
It tends not to cause symptoms early on, but at a later stage unexplained weight loss, swollen ankles, hands or feet, shortness of breath, fatigue, itchy skin, muscle cramps, nausea and headaches can all be a sign of the disease.
Separate analysis from the European pharmaceutical industry found type 2 diabetes currently costs the UK economy more than £3billion a year. Cardiovascular disease accounts for £2.6billion of this burden, while chronic kidney disease contributes a further £2.3billion.
items.title_zh: 三分之一的2型糖尿病患者将发展心脏或肾脏疾病
items.summary_zh: 研究表明，2型糖尿病患者的严重并发症随着时间的推移显著增加，尤其是肥胖、异常血脂、高血压和高血糖等因素对血管和重要器官造成的损害。研究结果强调了在最早机会内全面检测和治疗2型糖尿病的重要性，以帮助降低严重并发症的风险。通过及时的干预，可以有效减少心脏病和肾脏病等并发症的发生率，改善患者的整体健康状况。
items.l1_lead: 研究显示，三分之一的2型糖尿病患者可能发展为心脏或肾脏疾病，强调了早期检测和治疗的重要性以降低并发症风险。
items.l2_summary: 研究显示，约三分之一的2型糖尿病（Type 2 Diabetes）患者在其病程中将发展为心脏病或肾脏病等严重并发症。随着时间的推移，这些患者的并发症风险显著增加，尤其是肥胖、异常血脂、高血压和高血糖等因素对血管及重要器官的损害尤为明显。这些因素不仅影响患者的生活质量，还可能导致更为严重的健康问题。因此，研究强调了在最早机会内对2型糖尿病患者进行全面检测和治疗的重要性。通过及时的干预措施，可以有效降低心脏病和肾脏病等并发症的发生率，从而改善患者的整体健康状况。这一研究结果为临床实践提供了重要的指导，提醒医疗工作者在面对2型糖尿病患者时，应重视早期筛查和干预，以降低严重并发症的风险，提升患者的生活质量。

items.title: Take weight loss jabs to live for an extra decade, study suggests - Daily Mail
items.body:
原话：“Eating less over long periods reduces the burden placed on multiple organs, including the heart, liver, pancreas and kidneys, and may have broader health benefits on the brain and other tissues.”
论点：长期减少饮食可以减轻心脏、肝脏、胰腺和肾脏等多个器官的负担，并可能对大脑和其他组织有更广泛的健康益处。

quotes: Eating less over long periods reduces the burden placed on multiple organs, including the heart, liver, pancreas and kidneys, and may have broader health benefits on the brain and other tissues.
items.claim_zh: 长期减少饮食可以减轻心脏、肝脏、胰腺和肾脏等多个器官的负担，并可能对大脑和其他组织有更广泛的健康益处。
items.article_body:
By EMMA NELSON, HEALTH REPORTER and CIARAN FOREMAN, HEALTH REPORTER
Published: 11:00 EDT, 2 September 2026 | Updated: 11:36 EDT, 2 September 2026
Using weight loss injections in older age could extend a woman's life by roughly a decade, an intriguing study has suggested.
Blockbuster jabs like Ozempic and Mounjaro may be able to slow age-related body damage that accelerates death in women, when started around the age of 62.
Other benefits include improvements in memory, reduced inflammation and stabilised blood sugar.
The new findings add to previous research demonstrating the impact of calorie-restrictive diets on life span, scientists say.
Users of the drugs – of which there are believed to be around 2.5 million in the UK – eat less because the jabs mimic a hormone that triggers the sensation of feeling full.
The mice study, published in the journal Nature, also follows previous research suggesting the treatments may protect against a range of diseases in animals.
Experts believe the new findings on ageing could help explain why.
'Most chronic diseases are deeply rooted in the ageing process,' said Rafael de Cabo, senior investigator at the National Institutes of Health, which funded the research, and author of a commentary on its results.
Blockbuster jabs like Ozempic and Mounjaro may be able to slow the age-related body-wide damage that accelerates death in women, when started around the age of 62
'If GLP-1 agonists do indeed slow it down, then a wide range of clinical benefits is exactly what you'd expect to see.'
Naveed Sattar, professor of Cardiometabolic Medicine at the University of Glasgow, who was not involved in the study, added: 'Eating less over long periods reduces the burden placed on multiple organs, including the heart, liver, pancreas and kidneys, and may have broader health benefits on the brain and other tissues.'
To test the drugs' effects on ageing, scientists from the University of California, Berkeley, gave semaglutide – otherwise known as Wegovy or Ozempic – to female mice who'd lived 75 per cent of their lifespan, meaning they were 20-month-old female mice.
In human terms, this would be roughly equivalent to a 62-year-old woman starting treatment, experts said.
Compared with mice that did not receive the medicine, those given the drug for three months had improved muscle and brain function – key in protecting against diseases like dementia.
They also had lower levels of inflammation, better blood-sugar control and an improved ability to heal wounds – hallmarks of healthier ageing.
Mice that continued receiving the treatment until the end of their lives lived around 100 days longer.
Experts said this amounted to extending lifespan by around 11 per cent.
In the average British woman, who lives to around 83, the equivalent increase would amount to more than nine years of life.
To find out whether the benefits were caused by eating less, researchers compared the semaglutide-treated mice with another group given 24 per cent fewer calories.
While many of the effects were similar, the semaglutide-fed mice showed improvements in memory and blood sugar control – important for preventing diabetes.
'These differences point to the possibility that GLP-1 drugs tap into a biological pathway independent of calorie restriction,' said Danica Chen, corresponding author of the study and professor of metabolic biology and nutrition at University of California, Berkeley.
'Uncovering this potential route and the benefits that may stem from it is an important direction for future research into longevity-enhancing interventions.'
T he researchers stressed that the findings do not mean the drugs can immediately be considered life-extending for humans, and that further trials are required.
Scientists could eventually investigate whether the drugs benefit healthy older people – potentially opening the door to their use far beyond obesity and diabetes.
Dr Laura Sinclair, a lecturer in healthcare at the University of Exeter, who was not involved in the study, said the results are 'interesting'.
She continued: 'What we do know is that losing weight to be within a healthy range gives lots of health benefits, even if the individual later regains that weight. Naturally, the longer you maintain a healthy weight, the better for your biological ageing and risk of disease.'
Dr Sinclair added that there were reasons for caution, including potential risks of an older woman using semaglutide for the rest of her life.
Professor Tara Spires-Jones, division lead in the UK Dementia Research Institute at the University of Edinburgh, said: 'If these results from mice hold true in people, this is a promising hint that people taking [the drugs] may have an age-slowing benefit as well as benefits to reducing diabetes and obesity.'
But she added: 'The main limitations of this study are that while well-conducted, this experiment was in mice and only female mice.
'Mice are quite different from humans in many ways including lifespan and the range of environmental exposures of laboratory animals is limited.
'Women and men also have different physiology in ageing including factors such as the menopause.
'It will be interesting in the future to determine whether these results hold true in male mice and ultimately in people taking these drugs.'
items.title_zh: 减重注射可延长寿命十年，研究显示

items.l1_lead: 长期减少饮食可显著减轻多个器官负担，改善健康状况，研究表明可能延长寿命十年。

items.body:

论点：GLP-1药物对酒精成瘾的影响尚无数据，需要大规模试验验证其在酒精、暴食和抑郁症方面的益处。
