items.article_body:
SALA 2026, Day One: The annual South Asian Literature and Arts Festival (SALA) again drew an audience from far and wide. From almost the entire South Asian American community in California, anyone who could afford to walk, drive, ride, or fly to the venue had descended, like a flock of migrant birds, to the city of Atherton, where the festival was held September 26-27 on the grounds of Menlo College, unnoticed by students and faculty but much enjoyed by its regulars.
To some, it was a chance to see something new; for others, to reunite with old friends; to many, both. Also invited this year was the newly appointed Indian consul general in San Francisco, Satish Kumar Sivan.
The first act featured Kausar Munir, a lyricist and screenwriter for Yash Raj Films, Dharma Productions, Netflix, and Amazon, and the granddaughter of the renowned Urdu novelist Salma Siddiqui. Munir is also the first woman to win the Filmfare Award for Lyrics. She was introduced by the famous speaker and author Shikha Malaviya.
Before long, the auditorium was quite nearly a full house, and more than half the audience were paying attention, with the rule announced at the outset against personal video recording being broken only a dozen or so times.
The conversation proceeded at first along ordinary lines, with Munir saying she looks back on her previous creations either thinking her work might be better or being astounded at having written it so well, but prefers not to dwell on the past at all. When asked by Malaviya, “Where are you making a record? And where are you writing a love-letter?”, Munir gave no direct answer but explained her writing process, which seemed to serve that purpose admirably.
“It falls on a dialogue-writer… you have to make the plot… to be a bit of a performer,” said Munir. “There is no format… you have to feel your way through it”, and each collaboration between writer and director, she says, is different. Good directors are praised: “Amit Trivedi is… genuinely original… reacts very well to the script.”
“Do you have a favorite song you wrote?,” asked Malaviya. Munir replied, “Fun, party-songs are the most challenging to write, because you have no context.”
“Are lyrics poetry?” asked Malaviya, and Munir’s answer was essentially a ‘Yes’; but she places lyrics in a class by themselves, “because music and rhythm are important as words.”
“What does a poem mean to you, when you are writing a poem?,” asked Malaviya.
Munir replied, “This may sound Romantic;–– and I’m a fan of the Romantics! Shelley and Keats and Byron and all of them;–– it is a spontaneous expression of myself.”
Laughter and applause followed almost every remark, especially when Malaviya revealed, “The Internet thinks you’ve already written a book” (Munir protests she has no intention of writing one), “so we’re all waiting for it.”
When asked about the amalgam of languages in which her free verse is written, some of which she read aloud for the audience, Munir replied with the remark, worthy of passing into a proverb, “Jo zabaan bolté, Hindustani hé,” [“The language the people speak, is Hindustani].
Malaviya, author of Anandibai Joshee: A Life in Poems and co-founder of The (Great) Indian Poetry Collective, believes, “Everything women dream of, all they aspire to”; a recurring idea throughout various presentations all day.
In the next presentation, Dr. Venki Ramakrishnan, author of Why We Die, satisfies the audience’s need to learn from a Nobel laureate about ‘mortality’ and debunks the much-publicized efforts on the part of business magnates, after the fashion of powerful people since ancient times (his example is the Epic of Gilgamesh), to circumvent it.
In his lecture, Dr. Ramakrishnan makes comparisons across species, distinguishes life span from life expectancy, reminds us all of the basic premises of Natural Selection, and introduces the audience to the delicate balance every species must strike, with no two doing so identically, between the need of the individual for a long life and the need of the species for reproduction. Of interest to him is the idea of epigenetics, in which the most profound experiences of the individual may produce effects on its offspring, for example, the Dutch Famine and its effects on children born to those who suffered it.
Between such educational remarks, Dr. Ramakrishnan takes pains to dismiss what he calls “grand quackery”: namely, all popular claims about diets, fasts, cryonics, chemical treatments, and every other method of extending youth. “There are no long-term clinical trials,” he says, “and that’s what the science really needs.” His advice is simple: “Enjoy life; that’s going to make you live longer,” and, “Look at data carefully before spending money on supplements.”
Of disturbing interest to an anti-racist audience, Dr. Ramakrishnan informs us, “The same Body-Mass Index” may be normal in the European and excessive in the South Asian, African, or other diasporas, and this accounts for the latter appearing malnourished according to European or Euro-American measurements.
The last question came from a cryobiologist, who raised the possibility of using this technology for organ transplants; Dr. Ramakrishnan gently refuted this too.
At 3 p.m. in the Menlo College Student Union Building, the presentation on ‘Gaze from Nepal’ brought together the artists Tsherin Sherpa and Sneha Shrestha (better known as IMAGINE), both distinguished for combining ancient art with contemporary styles in pursuit of a new and global artistic ideal. Sherpa’s art has appeared at the Victoria & Albert Museum and the Asian Art Museum, and he himself appeared at the 2022 Venice Biennale, while IMAGINE’s art is the proud possession of the Harvard Art Museums and the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston. Moderator Padma Dorje brought them before a new viewing public, long accustomed to the work of artists and thinkers from other parts of the subcontinent, yet seldom privileged to see the rich heritage and cosmopolitan culture of modern-day Nepal.
Speaking first, Sherpa reminded the audience that traditional Nepali art is seen mostly in either religious or commercial settings, with nothing in between. He is the son of a traditional tankha artist, trained in the skills of his father from childhood, who set off early to make a name for himself as an artist of another kind, only to resume his ancestral art as the source of his own striking innovations: “to create”, he says, “a narrative… based on a more secular art… prayer flags” with a more human, even whimsical subject: one piece resembling a traditional prayer flag, but with advertising copy in the background disguised as prayer; a traditional Wrathful Deity design presented as a jumbled collage; another such design in an almost surrealist style; and a photograph of an abstract 3-dimensional installation.
Shrestha calls herself a lifelong artist, re-inspired by the idea of “letters as images” in street art in Boston, where she studied, and investigated Nepali traditions of calligraphy for its own sake: a form alive and well-known in the Arabic-writing world, but, IMAGINE says, deserving to be better known in Nepali Devanagari script. The audience was soon persuaded by examples of her work in a colorful slide show, from pages of translucent lettering in broad strokes on a solid-color background to brazen-colored panels of the Nepali kau, repeated, to the same in the form of a chandelier, to a mural six stories high, all meant, she said, to inspire still more such works in other artists. “At that point”, she says, “it belongs to the city, and that’s what I wanted.” Her sources, she says, vary from immigration forms to costumes worn by the artist’s elders.
IMAGINE concluded with a pavilion entitled ‘Why we Gather’ in Lo Manthang, Mustang, Nepal: a part of the world, she says, unused to rain; built to serve as a gathering hall for local people to discuss responses to the increasing rate of rainfall as a result of climate change. “To protect the living culture,” IMAGINE reminds us, “is also protecting the land.”
The next event, entitled ‘Desi Boys’, brought together Karan Mahajan, author of The Complex, and Aatish Taseer, author of Stranger to History, The Way Things Were, and The Temple-Goers, et al., moderated by Menlo College’s own Dr. Melissa Poulsen.
The two speakers are similar in appearance and manner, and played off one another’s speeches like a double act, each enlarging on the other’s remarks, talking along merrily like old friends, while the moderator, an example to moderators everywhere, kept both of them on the subject of their books and the status of Taseer as a political exile, his Overseas Citizenship of India recently revoked by the BJP government; to punish a satire, he says, of which he was the author, of Prime Minister Modi. “To lose one’s country is an intimate shame”, says Taseer. Mahajan adds, “OCI status can be taken away, but the Indian way of seeing the world cannot.”
Otherwise, Mahajan’s answers to most questions refer to his recent book, The Complex, which depicts the internal disagreements of a joint family in Delhi against the background of the larger internal disagreements of the Indian government shortly after Independence. Taseer contrasts longing for past glory with the American desire for “freedom” from the past; Mahajan adds, “All wish to be loved and understood… also a form of longing,” or of grievance.
In conclusion, the two speakers laugh at the presentation’s title of ‘Desi Boys’; Mahajan adds, referring to Taseer, “Pakistani Boy… but that’s Desi too.”
Final remarks ranged far and wide, especially on the part of Taseer, who claims to have known the last of the literary Schoenberg family, themselves friends of the great German writer Thomas Mann: exiles, like himself, with the subject and style of their writings forever altered and defined, as an audience question implied, by that exile.
Racism was also discussed. Taseer cites Shakespeare’s Tragedy of Othello and explains its antagonist ‘Iago’ as “an untalented mediocrity jealous of a talented outsider”; an archetype to explain, not Mahajan’s “Laxman Chopra” character alone, but nationalists and ethno-nationalists everywhere.
“Are the populations [within a nation] mixing?”, asks Mahajan, suggesting they are subject to discrimination and being forced out if not. Integration and assimilation were discussed at length by Mahajan, to the laughter and agreement, as with most of his remarks, of the audience. Taseer, meanwhile, informs us, In Buddhism, longing for the past, or for a lost home is a form of attachment, to be overcome by the disciplined seeker.
Shobhaa De, the last speaker for Day One, is the author of the largest number of books, and also the lightest reading; for her books depict neither the misfortunes of the Everyman nor the harrowing events of our century, but her own emotions, principally pleasures. Thus, she is the most fashionable of this year’s authors and offers a relief from the tragedies of the times, as well as a counterweight to the ascetic traditions of which the Indian diaspora is justly proud. “Indian culture”, according to De, is built for delight in food, clothes, music, and affection. This year, she was introduced and interviewed by Dr. Anjali Arondekar, another SALA regular.
“For me,” says De, “the voice is everything; I have to find it,” in every book she writes, of which there are now 28; “across genres”, says Arondekar. In this, she represents an exception to the usual rule, cited by Dr. Ramakrishnan today, that writers’ and artists’ imaginations decline after their middle years.
Like love poetry or erotic sculpture, De’s books remind us that the austerity of the spiritual and the delights of the sensual life can exist in the same tradition, time, and culture without endangering one another. “We have,” De says, “in a way, undermined and under-rated it [Sensuality]”; the rising generation is lost for words about eating, drinking, seeking a lover, and ot
items.title_zh: 南亚多元声音汇聚：从Kausar Munir到Venki Ramakrishnan
items.summary_zh: 本文探讨了南亚科学家在延长青春的饮食和冷冻技术等领域的观点，指出这些流行方法缺乏长期临床试验的支持。科学家们强调，科学研究需要更多的数据来验证这些方法的有效性。Kausar Munir提到：“没有长期临床试验，这正是科学所需。”而Venki Ramakrishnan则建议人们享受生活，以此来延长寿命。此外，科学家们还提醒消费者在购买补充剂前要仔细查看数据。这些观点共同指向了对科学研究和数据支持的迫切需求。
items.l1_lead: 南亚科学家呼吁对延长青春的饮食和冷冻技术进行更多长期临床试验，以验证其有效性，并提醒消费者关注数据支持。
items.l2_summary:
本文探讨了南亚科学家在延长青春的饮食和冷冻技术等领域的观点，强调这些流行方法缺乏长期临床试验的支持，亟需更多的数据来验证其有效性。Kausar Munir指出：“没有长期临床试验，这正是科学所需。”这一观点反映了科学界对数据支持的迫切需求，尤其是在涉及健康和寿命延长的领域。与此同时，诺贝尔奖得主Venki Ramakrishnan则提出了另一种生活态度，他建议人们应享受生活，以此来延长寿命。这一建议虽然与科学研究的严谨性有所不同，但也强调了生活质量的重要性。

科学家们还提醒消费者在购买补充剂时要仔细查看相关数据，以确保所选产品的安全性和有效性。这一警示进一步突显了科学研究在健康领域的重要性，尤其是在面对市场上众多未经验证的产品时。总的来说，南亚科学家们的观点共同指向了对科学研究和数据支持的迫切需求，呼吁在健康和营养领域的创新应建立在扎实的科学基础之上。

items.title: Nobelist Dr. Venki Ramakrishnan On Why We Die & Our Quest For Immortality - India Currents
items.body:
原话：“I was not actually a very good physicist.” / “I left physics because I didn’t think I would do very well in it as a career.” / “You can think of me as a failed physicist.”
论点：他认为自己在物理学方面并不出色，因此转向生物学。

quotes: I was not actually a very good physicist.

items.claim_zh: 他认为自己在物理学方面并不出色，因此转向生物学。
items.article_body:
One of the most popular sessions at the 2026 South Asian Literature and Art (SALA) Festival featured Nobel Laureate Dr. Venki Ramakrishnan in a discussion on “The Science of Death”, moderated by science journalist Angela Saini. The event, moderated by science journalist Angela Saini, was held at Menlo College, Atherton, CA on Sept 26 th .
Ramakrishnan’s book, Why We Die: The New Science of Aging and the Quest for Immortality, brings together biology, history, and ethics, blending scientific rigor and accessibility for a general audience. Kirkus Reviews called it “an illuminating account of the science of life extension with a more critical eye than most. “
In an exclusive interview with Raji Pillai for India Currents, Dr. Ramakrishnan discussed his journey, the next frontiers in science, and what lies ahead. This interview has been edited for brevity and clarity.
Raji Pillai: You studied physics in college in Baroda, and then went on to obtain a PhD in Physics. Tell us about your move.
Dr. Venki Ramakrishnan: I was not actually a very good physicist. I left physics because I didn’t think I would do very well in it as a career. I became interested in biology. In fact, I went back to graduate school to learn biology.
Physics is a beautiful, elegant subject. Exams weren’t hard for me, but research was: thinking like a physicist, breaking problems down and making real progress. The abstraction and mathematics just keep increasing. You can think of me as a failed physicist.
Biology is hard in a different way. It’s a highly complex system, and you must design experiments that extract information from it. But it has had huge breakthroughs in the last 75 years, so the move has been rewarding.
RP: How did you find your way to the UK, to the Medical Research Council Laboratory of Molecular Biology (LMB) in Cambridge?
VR: I went back to graduate school to learn biology. In my second year I wrote to Don Engelman at Yale, who had once offered me a postdoc I’d declined because I knew no biology: now I know some biology, and I even know what a ribosome is. He had no opening, but his collaborator Peter Moore, who worked on ribosomes, did. With very few publications and an odd career, for them to take a chance on me was remarkable. So I got into ribosomes almost by accident.
Ribosomes were out of fashion then. After completing my postdoctoral research, I sent out about 50 faculty applications and didn’t get a single interview. Don arranged a job at Oak Ridge National Laboratory, which I soon realized was a dead end. Fifteen months later, I moved to Brookhaven National Laboratory, where I really learned to be an independent scientist.
A turning point was a sabbatical from Brookhaven to the Medical Research Council (MRC) Laboratory of Molecular Biology (LMB) in Cambridge, the lab that pioneered so much, from DNA to the first protein structures. I learned crystallography there and realized it was actually possible to solve the structure of the whole ribosome. The LMB had no job, so I went to the University of Utah, a beautiful place with great colleagues. But US grants run three to five years, and I sensed this problem might take far longer.
So I wrote to the LMB again. They liked my ideas but had no space, which I took as a polite no. Weeks later, the director, Richard Henderson (2017 Nobel laureate in Chemistry), wrote that the space had materialized. It meant nearly halving my salary and my wife giving up her life in Utah. We went for a long walk and said, ‘Let’s just do it.’ That was 27 years ago. I’ve now lived in Cambridge longer than anywhere.”
Get stories like these directly in your inbox. Curated by us monthly to deliver the best of ours to you. Subscribe for free to our Arts & Culture newsletter - click here!
Skip the Scroll. Find nearby events you'll want spend time at and make new friends with our free weekly Events listing newsletter! Sign up here >>
RP: You went to a historic place where the structure of DNA was discovered by Watson and Crick in 1953, and years later, you made another historic discovery about the structure of the ribosome. So much has happened in terms of applications for DNA structure. Similarly, for ribosome structure, what do you see as potential applications?
VR: The ribosome is older than DNA. Without the need to make proteins, there’d be no need for DNA to store instructions for them. But DNA transformed biology by showing how information is stored and transmitted. The ribosome sits at the crossroads between genes and their products, converting information into proteins. It’s far more complicated but hasn’t captured the public imagination, partly because the double helix is simple and makes an instantly recognizable picture.
DNA’s structure was solved in 1953, but making proteins from recombinant DNA came only in the ’80s; then came PCR, and everything exploded. It took decades, and with the ribosome it may take longer. The obvious application is antibiotics, but the goal of making antibiotics that are very specific to bacteria, but don’t affect humans, is a harder problem. Nature has done it many times, but enzymes humans lack entirely may be better targets. Penicillin is the classic case: bacteria have cell walls, and we don’t. Further out, people are engineering ribosomes, and we might design new, precisely coded synthetic polymers. But I went into it for fundamental research reasons. RP: You said tech folks see all problems as digital. How do you see it?
VR: They believe everything in the analog world can be represented digitally, like pictures and sound. Maybe, but analog systems change dynamically. We don’t understand the brain well enough to represent it digitally, and aging involves cells, tissues, and the whole organism. I’m not sure they can just crank their computers and solve big problems. AI will be very powerful in chemistry, as AlphaFold shows, but may struggle with complex systems like biology. Then again, ten years ago I might have completely missed where AI is today.
RP: What do you see as the next few frontiers in science, broadly, or in biology?
VR: The big questions are perennial: how does the brain work, how did life arise from chemicals, what is the origin of the genetic code, how did handedness (chirality) develop, and how does an egg develop into an organism? These are tough problems, especially the origin of life. Even how the ribosome evolved is fuzzy. Early ribosomes may have been RNA only. How did you go from little random peptides to something that actually is stored as a genetic code, and then you can make the same peptide over and over again? That’s not at all clear. And so there are some big fundamental questions still left in biology.”
RP: How long did it take you to write and publish your book? And now that you have closed your lab at the LMB, what lies ahead for you?
VR: Why We Die took three to four years: about a year of research, reading and interviews, two years of writing, and a year of editing.
In my book, I didn’t mention GLP-1 drugs at all, because they were so recent. That is certainly an area where people are trying to do some work related to this whole class of caloric restriction drugs. They are not without side effects and a need for long term clinical trials.
I’m already 74. But I don’t really know. I just have to think about it. Many people make a long-term plan, and maybe I’m lazy mentally, or maybe I’m burned out. But I haven’t really given much thought to what I want to do for the next five years or so.
Raji Pillai lives in the SF Bay Area and writes at www.rajiwrites.com. This article was informed by her training and profession as a scientist .

items.title_zh: 拉马克里希南谈死亡与追求不朽的科学探索
items.summary_zh: 本文讨论了科学家Venki Ramakrishnan对死亡及人类追求不朽的看法。他自述并不认为自己是一位优秀的物理学家，因此选择转向生物学领域。他的观点反映了对生命科学的深刻理解，以及对人类存在意义的思考。虽然他在物理学上感到不如意，但在生物学的探索中，他寻求理解生命的本质和延续的可能性。通过对生命的研究，拉马克里希南希望揭示人类如何面对死亡以及追求长生不老的科学基础。
items.l1_lead: 拉马克里希南通过生物学探索，深入思考人类面对死亡的意义及追求不朽的科学基础。
items.l2_summary:
拉马克里希南（Venki Ramakrishnan）在对死亡及人类追求不朽的科学探索中，展现了他对生命科学的深刻理解和对人类存在意义的思考。尽管他自认为在物理学领域并不出色，因此转向生物学，但这并未影响他对科学的热情和对生命本质的探索。拉马克里希南的研究旨在揭示人类如何面对死亡，以及在科学层面上追求长生不老的可能性。他通过生物学的视角，探讨了生命的延续与死亡之间的关系，试图理解生命的基本特征和人类在面对终极命运时的态度。

在他的探索中，拉马克里希南不仅关注生物学的基本原理，还深入思考了人类对不朽的渴望。这种渴望不仅是生物学上的延续，更是哲学上的追求。他的观点反映了科学与人文的交融，强调了科学探索在理解生命意义方面的重要性。通过对生命现象的研究，拉马克里希南希望能够为人类提供一种新的视角，帮助我们更好地理解死亡的不可避免性以及如何在有限的生命中追求更深层次的存在价值。

总的来说，拉马克里希南的工作不仅是对生物学的探索，更是对人类存在的深刻反思。他的研究为我们提供了理解生命与死亡之间复杂关系的科学基础，激励着人们在面对生命的终结时，仍能保持对科学和生命意义的追求。

items.article_body:
Share Save Add as preferred on Google Melissa Hogenboom BBC/ Stephen Parker In the end, I overshot my target and ate a grand total of 51 plants.
Over the last two years, a new health goal has been growing in popularity. First there was 10,000 steps, then five a day . Now we're being encouraged to eat 30 plants per week.
The trend is based on a 2018 study . It found that people who reported eating at least 30 plants per week tended to have more biodiverse gut microbiomes compared to those who ate fewer than ten. Subsequent studies have found that changing your diet to incorporate this much flora each week can improve your microbiome .
This has many well-known benefits such as reducing inflammation and helping us to live healthier, longer lives .
However, when my editor suggested I give the 30-plants trend a go, it initially sounded extremely intimidating and perhaps impossible. I imagined preparing complicated salads for every meal and struggling with the vast quantities of fibre I'd be consuming. But one week on from my experiment, I can report that it was remarkably easy. So easy, in fact, that I accidentally overshot my goal and ended up eating 51 plants in total. Here's how.
First up, you don’t necessarily need 30 as your goal.
Rob Knight, director of the Center for Microbiome Innovation, at the University of California, San Diego, led the research which began the 30-plant trend. He says the number 30 is somewhat arbitrary, especially as there weren't many participants who ate over 30 plants per week in his study. Those who eat 25 or even 20 may also experience similar health benefits, he says.
Those who started with a low number of different plants saw the biggest effect. "If you're already eating a moderate number of plants, the effect is not going to be as large by adding more."
As it has grown in popularity, the goal of eating 30 plants has been gamified. Each additional plant earns you a " plant point ".
There are six main categories of food we can include, which are:
Tea, coffee and chocolate count too. All contain compounds, such as antioxidants, which can benefit our health.
The fact that spices are included surprised me. Research shows that adding a mix of spices to everyday meals can result in measurable improvements in gut microbes in as little as 48 hours, explains Federica Amati, a nutrition scientist at Imperial College, London.
Some sources suggest that herbs, spices, tea and coffee should count as a quarter of a point each.
Small changes can quickly affect our "microbe ecosystem" says Amati, but to make this meaningful, we need continued plant diversity.
The benefits of focusing on a diverse diet is that it pushes us past simply choosing the obvious, like apples, cucumbers and peppers, says Amati. Research has found that low consumption of whole grains, nuts and seeds is a leading risk factor for an early death.
Of course, hitting such a large range of different food items can be expensive if you buy lots of fresh produce, but for my experiment I used a mixture of fresh ingredients, cupboard staples as well as frozen food.
Each day of my experiment, I ate my usual bowl of overnight oats with chia seeds and yoghurt every morning for breakfast. This week I varied the fruits I added each day.
For lunch I rarely have much time, so I ate a sandwich or had leftovers from the night before, which also helped avoid waste.
I did put more thought into my evening meals than my usual on-the-day planning, because I was trying not to repeat the same ingredients. I picked recipes not too far from my routine but aimed for those that had plenty of plant-based ingredients.
My grocery shop looked slightly more colourful than usual, but it wasn't more expensive.
Monday: For dinner I had a chickpea tagine, which was delicious and quick to make. I followed this chickpea tagine recipe from BBC Good Food and added peas for an extra boost of fibre.
Plants today: Oats, blueberries, chia seeds, cabbage, peas, chickpeas, couscous, tomatoes, onions, raisins. Also today: Several spices (which I'm listing as one item).
Tuesday: Selena Wu, a dietician at King's College London, says that it helps to focus on what extra fibre you can add to a meal. That could involve adding some nuts or seeds into your breakfast cereal or eating a side salad with your sandwich, which is what I did at lunch today.
For dinner I made a quinoa salad with green lentils, asparagus and grilled salmon.
Plants today: Raspberries, satsuma, apple, quinoa, broccoli, spinach, asparagus, lemon, garlic, spring onions.
Wednesday: A simple curry is another staple in my household, but I tried a new recipe this time, adding sweet potatoes and red peppers, served with green beans on the side. The whole family enjoyed this one and it contained plenty of spices.
Plants today: Coffee, banana, cashew nuts, coconut milk, sweet potato, green beans, red peppers, brown rice.
Thursday: By Thursday I've already hit close to 30 so the pressure is off but I'm still adding as much variation as I can and sticking to my meal plan.
Today I chose something easy that I could put together quickly using vegetables and cupboard staples. I made a vegetable soup with onions, garlic carrots, lentils and sweet potatoes and served it with a slice of sourdough bread and a simple side salad.
I also made a delicious healthy frozen banana milkshake , to which I added cocoa powder and cashew nuts.
Plants today: Tea, cocoa powder, cashew nuts, pumpkin seeds, red lentils, rocket salad.
Friday: As the week went on, keeping up with the variety became more challenging, as I can't count the same item twice, but I still aimed to add plenty of fresh produce even if it meant repeating items. It's also hard to keep track of quite how many spices and herbs I've eaten.
Friday was taco day , a popular dish in our house, which I made with black beans and beef mince. Luckily my "ready to eat" avocados were finally ripe, so I made a large portion of guacamole as well as a salsa.
Plants today: Wholemeal wheat wraps, cucumber, black beans, avocado, fresh coriander.
Saturday: Our Saturdays are always busy so I wanted a very quick simple meal I could throw together. I made a simple noodle stir fry using tempeh, which is made from fermented cooked soya beans, but any protein would suit. My kids didn't like this one (and I'm not convinced I cooked the tempeh to perfection as it was a little bitter) so I made a simple pasta at the same time.
Plants today : Dried mango, peanuts, tempeh, olives, pak choi, baby corn, sesame seeds.
Sunday: By Sunday my enthusiasm for cooking so many new meals had started to fade. I let my oven do the hard work and made a chicken and vegetable tray bake with a side salad.
I managed to last the week without a top-up shop and I raided my fridge to introduce something new. I still had aubergines, courgettes and potatoes and defrosted some chicken thighs.
Plants today : Carrots, aubergine, courgettes, potatoes.
In the end, my plant tally for the week came to about 51. The main challenge was the planning, as well as the difficulty of cooking new recipes after a busy day. But those problems will disappear once I've repeated these recipes again a few times.
I also had a lot more leftovers than usual, which served as healthy lunches for the next day. I snacked less and didn't eat out, which is where the real saving came in. My children, often quite fussy, tried more than they usually would too.
The biggest surprise is that in the end, I was over-prepared. I could almost have hit 30 plant points by just cooking my usual meals. Once you add in coffee, tea, chocolate, spices, and wholegrains, it's remarkable how quickly you get to 30 plants if you already have a healthy diet.
But one thing I will keep doing is pushing myself to vary the ingredients I buy each week. And keeping an eye out for opportunities to throw an extra plant in any meal. At the very least, my cupboard is now full of nuts and seeds that I will continue to sprinkle onto everything.
* Melissa Hogenboom is a senior health correspondent at the BBC. She is melissa_hogenboom on Instagram.

items.title_zh: 我尝试每周吃30种植物，结果出乎意料的简单
items.summary_zh: 本文探讨了每周摄入超过30种植物的健康益处，核心论点是，增加植物种类的健康效果并不显著，20或25种植物也能带来类似的健康效果。研究指出，参与者中实际吃超过30种植物的人并不多，而那些开始时植物种类较少的人，其健康改善效果更为明显。这表明，适量增加植物摄入可能比追求数量更为重要。
items.l1_lead: 每周摄入超过30种植物的健康益处并不显著，适量增加植物种类比追求数量更为重要。
items.l2_summary:
本文探讨了每周摄入超过30种植物（plant）的健康益处，研究的核心论点是，增加植物种类的健康效果并不显著，实际上，摄入20或25种植物也能带来类似的健康效果。研究发现，参与者中实际吃超过30种植物的人并不多，而那些开始时植物种类较少的人，其健康改善效果更为明显。这一发现表明，适量增加植物摄入可能比追求数量更为重要。

在研究中，参与者的饮食习惯被仔细记录，结果显示，尽管许多人尝试增加植物的种类，但真正能够达到30种的比例并不高。这意味着，许多人在追求多样化的过程中可能会感到压力，而实际上，适度的植物摄入就能带来健康益处。研究强调，特别是对于那些起初植物摄入量较低的人，增加植物种类的摄入能够显著改善他们的健康状况。

此外，研究还指出，植物的种类虽然重要，但更关键的是整体饮食的均衡与多样性。参与者在增加植物种类的过程中，往往忽视了其他营养成分的摄入，导致整体饮食结构的不合理。因此，追求数量并不是唯一的健康策略，适量增加植物的摄入，结合均衡的饮食，可能更有助于提升健康水平。

综上所述，研究结果提示我们，在追求健康饮食时，适度增加植物种类的摄入比单纯追求数量更为重要。对于那些植物摄入量较少的人，逐步增加植物的种类和数量，将更有助于改善健康状况，而不必过于焦虑于达到30种植物的目标。

items.l2_summary:
本文探讨了微生物组（microbiome）在增强肌肉和促进健康老龄化中的重要作用，提出微生物组可以被视为一个器官，能够向身体其他部分发出信号，指示何时适合健康生长。研究表明，当微生物组的状态良好时，它会向身体发送信号，表明一切正常，适合健康成长；而在饥荒或不利条件下，微生物组则会发出警告信号。这一发现强调了微生物组在力量训练和整体健康中的关键角色，提示我们关注肠道健康，以促进身体的强壮与活力。

微生物组的健康状况直接影响到肌肉的增强和力量的保持，尤其是在不同年龄段的人群中。随着年龄的增长，肌肉质量和力量往往会下降，而良好的微生物组状态能够帮助减缓这一过程，促进肌肉的合成和修复。因此，维护微生物组的健康不仅有助于增强肌肉力量，还能改善整体的身体机能和生活质量。

此外，微生物组的多样性和组成也与个体的饮食、生活方式密切相关。通过合理的饮食和适当的锻炼，可以有效改善微生物组的状态，从而促进肌肉的增强和力量的保持。因此，关注肠道健康，优化微生物组的组成，成为了增强肌肉和保持力量的重要策略。

综上所述，微生物组在肌肉增强和健康老龄化中扮演着至关重要的角色，良好的微生物组状态不仅能够促进健康成长，还能帮助人们在各个年龄段保持力量和活力。因此，重视肠道健康，采取科学的饮食和锻炼方式，将是实现身体强壮与活力的重要途径。

items.l2_summary:
在职场中，工作质量的重要性不容忽视。本文探讨了如何成为更好的同事，强调了重视工作质量比追求个人声誉更为关键。作者指出，认真做好自己的工作所获得的回报往往会超越个人的声誉。这一观点提醒我们，真正的成就源于对工作的投入与执行，而非外界的评价。通过专注于自身的职业表现，职场人士能够实现更高的职业回报。

在现代职场环境中，许多人往往过于关注外界对自己的评价，试图通过建立声誉来获得认可。然而，作者强调，声誉的建立是建立在实际工作表现之上的，只有通过高质量的工作，才能赢得同事和上司的尊重与信任。工作质量不仅体现在完成任务的效率上，更体现在对工作的认真态度和对细节的关注。高质量的工作能够提升团队的整体表现，进而推动个人职业发展的良性循环。

此外，文章还提到，职场人士应当将重心放在提升自身技能和专业素养上，而不是单纯追求外在的认可。通过不断学习和实践，提升工作质量，最终将会在职业生涯中获得更丰厚的回报。作者的论点强调了在职场中，真正的成功来自于对工作的热情与投入，而非对声誉的盲目追求。

总之，重视工作质量是成为更好同事的关键。通过专注于自身的职业表现，职场人士不仅能够提升个人能力，还能为团队和组织创造更大的价值。最终，真正的成就将会在于对工作的认真态度和高质量的执行，而非外界的评价和声誉。

items.l1_lead: 定期力量训练和良好的肠道健康对老年人维持肌肉质量和整体健康至关重要，促进健康老龄化。
items.l2_summary: 随着年龄的增长，保持肌肉质量和力量变得愈发重要。本文探讨了肠道健康、力量训练（strength training）与健康老龄化之间的意外联系，强调了老年人需要增加运动量以维持健康。研究表明，定期进行力量训练对老年人的身体机能具有显著的积极影响，能够改善肌肉质量并提升整体健康水平。具体而言，积极的运动不仅有助于增强肌肉力量，还能促进心血管健康、改善代谢功能以及提升心理健康。因此，保持活跃的生活方式对于促进健康老龄化至关重要。通过这些研究，科学家们指出，老年人应当重视力量训练的实施，以应对衰老带来的身体机能下降，从而提高生活质量。总之，增强肌肉与保持力量不仅是老年人健康的关键，也是实现健康老龄化的重要途径。

在现代职场中，职业责任与个人生活之间的冲突日益显著，这一问题对同事之间的关系和工作效率产生了深远的影响。本文深入探讨了这一现象，强调了在工作环境中平衡专业与个人生活的重要性。作者通过节目讨论，指出许多员工在面对工作压力时，常常感到难以兼顾家庭、健康和个人兴趣等方面的需求，这种冲突不仅影响了他们的心理健康，也降低了工作效率。

文章最后呼吁，关注职业与个人冲突的问题不仅有助于提升工作环境的和谐性，还能显著提高整体生产力。通过建立一个更加包容和理解的工作氛围，企业和员工都能在各自的角色中获得更大的满足感与成就感，从而实现个人与职业的双赢。

items.title: Scientists construct a 'family tree' containing 1.28 million cells from a single embryo - Yahoo
items.body:
原话：“our dream of comprehensively mapping mammalian development.”
论点：该研究使团队更接近全面绘制哺乳动物发育的梦想。
items.attribution_basis: Google News 全名命中 + LLM 同一人核验（Yahoo） + 论点方向独立复核
quotes: our dream of comprehensively mapping mammalian development.
items.topic_zh: 构建哺乳动物发育的综合地图
items.claim_zh: 该研究使团队更接近全面绘制哺乳动物发育的梦想。
items.article_body:
DNA Typewriter reconstructs a 1.28-million-cell lineage tree in a mouse embryo, revealing ancestry and unequal developmental contributions. (CREDIT: The Brighter Side of News) DNA Typewriter helped reconstruct a lineage tree containing 1.28 million cells from a single developing mouse embryo.
The first two cells contributed unequal numbers of descendants but highly similar proportions of cell types.
The tree reveals developmental patterns, but covers only about 10% of the embryo and requires confirmation in independent animals.
Every cell in a developing animal has a history, but ordinary laboratory measurements usually erase that history. A molecular recorder has now helped recover it for more than a million cells in one mouse embryo.
The resulting family tree connects 1,281,141 sampled cells to their ancestry, reaching back to the fertilized egg. It follows development through 13.5 days, when organs have taken shape, and represents about 10% of the embryo's cells.
Published in Science , the work comes from the Seattle Hub for Synthetic Biology . The partnership brings together the Allen Institute, UW Medicine and Biohub . Jay Shendure, the hub's scientific director and a UW genome sciences professor, helped lead the study.
The achievement is a large, time-calibrated reconstruction, rather than a complete film of development. It reveals how lineages expand and become associated with particular tissues, while leaving important gaps in the record.
Circular lineage tree of a 13-day old mouse embryo originating from a single cell at the center expanding outward over developmental time. Cells derived from the first cell division are marked in blue or red. (CREDIT: Seattle Hub for Synthetic Biology)
DNA Typewriter uses prime editing to insert short sequences into engineered DNA recording sites, called tapes. Each insertion closes one position and activates the next, preserving the order in which symbols were written.
When a cell divides, its daughters inherit the existing record. Later edits distinguish their descendants, allowing researchers to infer relationships from shared histories. The recorder accumulates marks during development; it does not necessarily write one stamp for every division.
That ordered design helps address problems with earlier recording systems. Methods that cut both DNA strands can delete neighboring records. DNA Typewriter avoids requiring those double-strand breaks, although its records still contain missing data and unexpected edits.
The researchers injected the recording components into fertilized mouse eggs and collected embryos at 13.5 days. One embryo with strong recording activity became the focus of the detailed reconstruction. Its genome contained eleven independently recording tapes.
To retrieve their contents, the team redesigned the tapes to produce circular RNA transcripts. This made the records easier to recover alongside measurements of gene activity.
Scientists profiled nuclei rather than whole cells, helping avoid biases caused by separating mature tissues into individual cells. After quality checks, they obtained gene-expression profiles from 1,584,848 nuclei. Comparing those profiles with an existing mouse-development atlas identified the cells' types.
GIF shows cell lineage of mouse embryo, from fertilized egg to day 13.5 of development. Distance from the center is developmental time. (CREDIT: Seattle Hub for Synthetic Biology)
A strong burst of editing near the first division created distinct records in the embryo's two founding cells. Their descendants could therefore be assigned to two broad branches, which the researchers analyzed separately.
"We were surprised by just how robustly marking happened right at the very first division," said co-first author Haedong Kim. Those early marks provided an unusually clear starting point for the reconstruction.
Among cells with recovered recording data, about 57.1% were assigned to one founder and 41.9% to the other. Approximately 1% lacked an unambiguous assignment.
Despite that numerical imbalance, the two branches had highly similar cell-type compositions. One contributed more sampled descendants overall, without appearing disproportionately committed to a particular fate.
This finding applies to the embryo itself. Extraembryonic tissues were discarded, so the experiment cannot establish how the founders contributed to those supporting tissues.
Comparing the two branches also helped test whether developmental patterns recurred within the animal. That provides a useful internal check, but it cannot replace repeating the experiment in separate embryos.
GIF illustrates how DNA Typewriter works. It uses a prime editor to write a short DNA "symbol" into one active site on an engineered stretch of DNA. Each insertion closes that site and opens the next one, so the symbols read left to right in the order they were written. (CREDIT: Seattle Hub for Synthetic Biology)
The more striking inequality appeared later, around gastrulation, when the embryo establishes its major body layers. Researchers examined 3,849 reconstructed ancestral lineages dated to seven days after fertilization.
Just 170 of those lineages accounted for half the cells in the final tree. A simple model of neutral growth would have required about 720 lineages to supply the same share.
The analysis suggests that unequal contributions developed rapidly and largely plateaued by approximately day nine. It offers a timeline for a phenomenon often studied within individual tissues: some ancestors leave far more descendants than others.
The tree cannot determine whether larger families resulted from faster division, better survival or both. It records surviving lineages, without capturing cells that died along the way.
Spatial position may also matter. By day seven, ancestors occupy different parts of the embryo, where local signals can influence growth and fate. A large contribution therefore does not establish an inherited advantage or a predetermined tissue identity.
Close relatives in the tree often shared a cell type. Across the sampled data, 51% of neighboring sibling pairs had matching identities, about 9.4 times the frequency expected after randomly rearranging labels.
GIF illustrates DNA Typewriter's recorder, with bursts of edits over the 13.5-day period. (CREDIT: Seattle Hub for Synthetic Biology)
These are tree siblings, not necessarily two daughters of the same observed division. With only a fraction of cells sampled, the nearest available relatives may have missing family members between them.
Broader groups of related cells nevertheless recovered recognizable developmental organization. Their patterns corresponded to blood formation, nervous-system development and other major tissue groupings.
The researchers also used the reference atlas to estimate ancestral gene-expression states . Selected inferred paths resembled established developmental transitions, including the progression toward kidney progenitor cells.
Those ancestral states were computationally estimated, not directly recorded or independently validated. They are exploratory additions to the lineage tree, rather than observations of what every ancestor was doing.
Building the tree required two computational stages. A backbone contained 655,701 cells with more complete records. Another 625,440 were placed near their closest recorded relatives , expanding coverage while adding uncertainty about exact branching positions.
Timing also depends on assumptions. Editing accelerated early, slowed sharply, then recovered around gastrulation. Rates differed between cell types, particularly blood cells, so branch dates are approximations.
PNI of DNA Typewriter components identifies an E13.5 embryo with robust levels of sequential editing. (CREDIT: Jay Shendure et al, Science 2026)
The recorder itself may have affected biology. Although broad stress and damage signals were not elevated, some genes near insertion sites changed expression. The researchers cannot yet determine how those changes influenced the tree.
Shendure said the work brings the team closer to "our dream of comprehensively mapping mammalian development." Such maps could eventually provide references for investigating birth defects , cancer and other conditions in which cellular development changes.
This experiment did not test a disease treatment or establish how a human disorder begins. Its immediate contribution is a resource for studying normal development, with explicit limits on sampling, timing and reproducibility.
The tree is available through NextCell , an interactive browser for exploring cellular ancestry. Independent animals, additional developmental stages and improved recorders will be needed to turn this first large reconstruction into a reliable account of mammalian development.
These resources explain the recording technology and the developmental references that make cellular family trees useful.
A time-resolved, multi-symbol molecular recorder via sequential genome editing : Introduces DNA Typewriter and demonstrates ordered molecular recording in living mammalian cells. (Nature, 2022)
Molecular recording using DNA Typewriter : Describes the experimental workflow for recording the order of molecular events with sequential DNA editing. (Nature Protocols, 2024)
A single-cell time-lapse of mouse prenatal development from gastrula to birth : Provides the gene-expression atlas used to identify cell types and explore inferred ancestral states. (Nature, 2024)
Single-cell, whole-embryo phenotyping of mammalian developmental disorders : Shows how large-scale cellular profiling can reveal developmental changes in genetically altered mouse embryos. (Nature, 2023)
Whole-organism lineage tracing by combinatorial and cumulative genome editing : Demonstrates an earlier genome-editing approach to reconstructing cell ancestry in zebrafish. (Science, 2016)
Research findings are available online in the journal Science .
The original story " Scientists construct a 'family tree' containing 1.28 million cells from a single embryo " is published in The Brighter Side of News.

items.title_zh: 科学家构建包含128万个细胞的胚胎“家谱”
items.summary_zh: 一项新研究中，科学家们成功构建了一个包含128万个细胞的“家谱”，这些细胞均来源于一个单一的胚胎。这项研究使团队更接近于全面绘制哺乳动物（mammal）发育的梦想。研究者们希望通过这一成果，深入理解哺乳动物的发育过程，为未来的生物医学研究提供重要的基础数据和理论支持。
items.l1_lead: 科学家成功构建了一个包含128万个细胞的胚胎“家谱”，为深入理解哺乳动物发育过程提供了重要基础数据。
items.l2_summary:
在一项新研究中，科学家们成功构建了一个包含128万个细胞的“家谱”，这些细胞均来源于一个单一的胚胎。这一突破性成果使研究团队更接近于全面绘制哺乳动物（mammal）发育的梦想，标志着在理解复杂生物发育过程方面的重要进展。通过对这些细胞的系统性分析，研究者们希望能够深入理解哺乳动物的发育机制，这对于未来的生物医学研究具有重要的基础数据和理论支持。

该研究不仅展示了科学家们在细胞追踪和发育生物学领域的技术进步，还为探索细胞如何在胚胎发育过程中相互作用提供了新的视角。128万个细胞的“家谱”将为研究细胞分化、组织形成及器官发育等关键过程提供丰富的信息。这种细致的细胞图谱能够帮助科学家们揭示不同细胞类型的起源及其在发育过程中的角色，从而为理解疾病机制和开发新的治疗方法奠定基础。

总之，这项研究的成功不仅是对哺乳动物发育过程的深入探索，也为未来的生物医学研究提供了重要的理论依据和数据支持，推动了我们对生命科学的理解。

items.article_body:
Kidney disease can develop before heart failure in people newly diagnosed with type 2 diabetes, according to new research reported by Knowridge. The study analysed data from nearly 1.62 million adults.
The findings were presented at the annual meeting of the European Association for the Study of Diabetes, held in Milan from 28 September to 2 October. The study was led by Dr Naveed Sattar of the University of Glasgow in the UK.
The researchers examined which complication occurred first after a diagnosis of type 2 diabetes. Within five years, 19.0 per cent of patients had developed chronic kidney disease first, compared with 8.3 per cent who developed heart failure first.
The relationship between the two organs was found to work in both directions. Among people with chronic kidney disease, 22.7 per cent developed heart failure within five years. Among those with heart failure, 42.0 per cent developed chronic kidney disease over the following five years.
When chronic kidney disease, heart failure and death were considered together, the risk was 32.9 per cent within five years of a type 2 diabetes diagnosis. After 10 years, it had risen to 55.1 per cent.
Chronic kidney disease means that the kidneys gradually lose their ability to filter waste products and excess fluid from the blood. In its early stages, it can cause few noticeable symptoms, making blood and urine tests important for detecting it.
According to Sattar, complications can build up over time as high blood sugar, high blood pressure, unhealthy blood fat levels and obesity damage blood vessels and vital organs. He stressed the importance of detecting and treating type 2 diabetes as early and comprehensively as possible.
The findings describe risk across a large population and cannot predict what will happen to an individual. They were presented at a scientific meeting, so the full published study and the methods used in the research should also be taken into account when assessing the evidence. | BGNES
items.title_zh: 研究发现2型糖尿病患者肾病早于心力衰竭出现
items.summary_zh: 一项研究指出，在2型糖尿病患者中，高血糖、高血压、不健康的血脂水平和肥胖等因素会导致肾脏疾病在心力衰竭之前出现。研究数据显示，在五年内，19.0%的患者首先发展为慢性肾脏疾病，而8.3%的患者则首先发展为心力衰竭。这一发现强调了尽早、全面检测和治疗2型糖尿病的重要性，以减少并发症的发生。

items.l2_summary: 一项针对2型糖尿病患者的研究发现，肾脏疾病的发生往往早于心力衰竭（heart failure）。研究指出，高血糖、高血压、不健康的血脂水平以及肥胖等因素是导致这一现象的主要原因。在观察的五年内，19.0%的患者首先发展为慢性肾脏疾病（chronic kidney disease），而只有8.3%的患者首先发展为心力衰竭。这一数据表明，肾脏疾病在2型糖尿病患者中更为常见且更早出现，提示临床医生在管理糖尿病患者时，应更加关注肾脏健康。研究结果强调了对2型糖尿病患者进行早期、全面的检测和治疗的重要性，以减少肾脏疾病及其他并发症的发生。这一发现不仅为临床实践提供了重要的参考依据，也为未来的研究方向指明了道路，促使医疗界更加重视糖尿病患者的肾脏健康管理。

items.title_zh: Tirzepatide对糖尿病患者心血管保护的影响
items.summary_zh: 本文讨论了Tirzepatide（Tisepathy）在糖尿病患者中的应用，强调其对心血管疾病的保护作用。科学家Naveed Sattar指出，Tirzepatide为糖尿病患者提供了心血管保护的信心，帮助他们更好地应对糖尿病与心血管疾病共存的挑战。关键证据是美国食品药品监督管理局（FDA）已批准Tirzepatide作为糖尿病患者的心血管保护药物。这一批准为临床实践提供了重要支持，表明Tirzepatide在改善糖尿病患者的整体健康状况方面具有潜力。
items.l1_lead: Tirzepatide被FDA批准用于糖尿病患者，显示出其在心血管保护方面的潜力，为患者应对糖尿病与心血管疾病的共存提供了信心。
items.l2_summary:
Tirzepatide（Tisepathy）是一种新型药物，近年来在糖尿病患者中的应用引起了广泛关注，尤其是在其对心血管疾病的保护作用方面。科学家Naveed Sattar指出，Tirzepatide为糖尿病患者提供了心血管保护的信心，帮助他们更有效地应对糖尿病与心血管疾病共存的挑战。值得注意的是，美国食品药品监督管理局（FDA）已批准Tirzepatide作为糖尿病患者的心血管保护药物，这一批准为临床实践提供了重要支持，表明Tirzepatide在改善糖尿病患者的整体健康状况方面具有显著潜力。

这一研究强调了Tirzepatide在心血管保护方面的关键作用，尤其是在糖尿病患者中，心血管疾病的风险普遍较高。通过临床试验和研究数据，Tirzepatide被证明能够有效降低心血管事件的发生率，从而为糖尿病患者的心血管健康提供了新的治疗选择。这一发现不仅为患者带来了希望，也为医生在治疗糖尿病患者时提供了新的思路和方法。

总的来说，Tirzepatide的批准和应用标志着糖尿病治疗领域的一次重要进展，尤其是在心血管保护方面的潜力，能够帮助患者更好地管理他们的健康状况，降低心血管疾病的风险。这一研究成果为未来的临床实践奠定了基础，推动了糖尿病与心血管疾病的综合管理策略的发展。

items.article_body:
Losing weight is hard. Very hard. Indeed, research suggests that only around 20 per cent of people who intentionally lose a significant amount of weight through dieting manage to keep it off for at least a year.
However, the emergence of glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist drugs has made this battle easier. By dramatically reducing people’s hunger drive, these drugs have made substantial weight loss achievable for the estimated 40 million adult users in the US.
Few medicines have transformed public health this quickly. Within just a few years of GLP-1 drugs becoming mainstream, the US adult obesity rate has begun to fall for the first time since records began .
But evidence is rapidly emerging that the effects go far beyond appetite suppression and weight loss. As researchers have studied millions of people taking GLP-1 drugs, they’ve uncovered a growing list of unexpected effects – some remarkably promising, others potentially concerning.
It might not just be our cravings for food that GLP-1s can help treat – they could blunt addiction across the board.
A major study of 600,000 US veterans, published in The BMJ , found that GLP-1 use was associated with a lower risk of substance use disorders involving alcohol, nicotine, cannabis, cocaine and opioids.
The researchers also looked at 524,817 participants who did not have a substance use disorder at the start of the study. Those taking GLP-1 medications were 14 per cent less likely to develop one than people taking other diabetes and weight-loss medications.
And among the participants who already had a substance use disorder, GLP-1 use was associated with 12 fewer serious addiction-related events per 1,000 users.
The authors suggest that GLP-1 treatment can “blunt that craving that pulls people toward whatever they’re addicted to”.
However, Naveed Sattar , professor of cardiometabolic medicine at the University of Glasgow, cautions that this kind of observational data isn’t the same as proving GLP-1s cause a drop in addiction.
“Other than for alcohol , we don’t yet have the data. We need big trials to validate the benefits in alcohol addiction and trials, too, to investigate the benefits for binge-eating and depression,” he says.
Although much of the cardiovascular benefit of GLP-1s stems from weight loss, mounting evidence suggests the drugs also have direct protective effects in people who have already experienced a heart attack or stroke.
For instance, in one trial of over 17,000 patients, those given semaglutide were 20 per cent less likely to have a further heart attack, stroke or cardiovascular death than those given a placebo. Tellingly, this benefit appeared before patients had lost a meaningful amount of weight.
A follow-up analysis found the cardioprotective effect was independent of how much weight patients actually lost, suggesting GLP-1s act directly on the heart and blood vessels rather than simply working through weight loss.
Exactly how the drug does this, however, is less certain. One theory is that the drugs have anti-inflammatory effects , calming immune cells in the bloodstream and lowering markers of inflammation.
Chronic inflammation can cause plaques to build up on blood vessels, creating a blockage that can cause a heart attack or stroke. By reducing this inflammation, the drugs help keep blood vessels clear and relax artery walls. And there are clinical trials to back these claims.
“We know that they affect blood pressure, which is a key risk factor in cardiovascular disease,” says Sattar.
Early studies suggest that dementia and other brain diseases stand to benefit from GLP-1s.
These include a recent major review of 30 studies that found the drugs reduced the build-up of amyloid-beta and tau – two proteins that can damage and kill brain cells in Alzheimer’s – in animals.
Human evidence is earlier-stage but promising in places. One trial of GLP-1 drug liraglutide in 204 people with mild to moderate Alzheimer’s found patients on the drug had a slower decline on cognitive tests and 50 per cent less brain volume loss than those on a placebo.
However, the wider clinical evidence is mixed. Extensive clinical trials published in The Lancet found that semaglutide taken in the form of pills did not slow memory or functional decline in patients with early Alzheimer’s disease over two years.
The overall picture suggests GLP-1 drugs do affect the brain in some way. Exactly what they’re doing, however (and how they’re doing it) remains unclear.
As University of Cambridge neuroendocrinologist Prof Giles Yeo previously told us , drug companies have “no freaking clue” what GLP-1s are doing in our brains.
You might expect people who lose weight to become more active. Yet research analysing smartwatch data suggests the opposite may happen for some GLP-1 users, who appear to exercise less after starting the drugs.
On average, participants walked around 560 fewer steps a day after beginning treatment, with their daily step count falling from 5,047 to 4,487. Time spent doing moderate-to-vigorous exercise also dropped, from 28 minutes to 22 minutes a day.
However, obesity expert Dr Marie Spreckley at the University of Cambridge thinks the results should be treated with some caution.
“Because this was an observational analysis, it cannot establish that the medication itself caused the reduction in activity,” she says. She notes, too, that some people experience nausea, gastrointestinal symptoms or fatigue, which could temporarily reduce their activity levels.
“The findings reinforce something we already know: medication works best as part of comprehensive obesity care,” she says. “Maintaining physical activity during weight loss is important not only for cardiovascular health, but also for preserving muscle strength, physical function and independence.”
GLP-1 drugs also appear to affect our bones, something that initially surprised researchers. Whether they’re ultimately good or bad for the skeleton, however, remains uncertain.
Some studies suggest GLP-1 drugs may strengthen bones by acting on the cells that maintain bone tissue, slowing bone breakdown while stimulating the formation of new bone.
Separately, early evidence (mostly from animal studies) suggests the drugs could offer a potential treatment for osteoarthritis.
However, somewhat confusingly, other studies suggest the treatments can lower bone density.
Research from the University of Colorado linked GLP-1s to an increased fracture risk in obese patients without diabetes, particularly in those with a body mass index (BMI) over 40 and aged over 68.
That doesn’t necessarily mean the drugs are directly weakening bones, though. Rapid weight loss is known to reduce bone mineral density, and losing muscle at the same time can make people less stable on their feet. Together, those changes could leave some people more vulnerable to falls and broken bones.
“[This research] has understandably raised questions about the potential long-term effects of GLP-1 receptor agonists on skeletal health,” Spreckley says.
But, she notes, weight loss itself can improve osteoarthritis symptoms in people living with obesity by reducing strain on joints.
“I think the key message is that the goal should be healthy weight loss rather than simply maximum weight loss,” she says.

items.title_zh: Tirzepatide降低心血管事件，C-Peptide对T1D进展的见解
items.summary_zh: 本文讨论了Tirzepatide在降低心血管事件方面的效果，以及C-Peptide在1型糖尿病（T1D）进展中的作用。研究表明，Tirzepatide相比安慰剂确实降低了心血管事件的发生率，多个分析方法的结果均显示出显著的心血管风险降低。此外，Emily Sims的研究提供了C-Peptide在糖尿病进展过程中的重要见解，强调了其在监测和理解T1D进展中的潜在价值。这些发现为临床实践提供了新的视角，可能影响未来的治疗策略。
items.l1_lead: Tirzepatide显著降低心血管事件发生率，同时C-Peptide在1型糖尿病进展中提供了重要见解，可能影响未来的治疗策略。
items.l2_summary:
本文探讨了Tirzepatide在降低心血管事件方面的效果，以及C-Peptide（C肽）在1型糖尿病（T1D）进展中的作用。研究结果表明，Tirzepatide相较于安慰剂显著降低了心血管事件的发生率，多个分析方法的结果均显示出心血管风险的显著降低。这一发现为临床实践提供了新的视角，可能会影响未来的治疗策略。

此外，Emily Sims的研究为C-Peptide在糖尿病进展过程中的重要性提供了深入见解。C-Peptide作为胰岛素分泌的标志物，其水平的变化能够反映胰腺β细胞的功能状态，从而为监测和理解T1D的进展提供了潜在的价值。通过对C-Peptide的研究，能够更好地评估T1D患者的病情变化，进而为个体化治疗方案的制定提供依据。

综上所述，Tirzepatide在心血管事件预防方面的积极效果，以及C-Peptide在T1D进展监测中的重要作用，均为糖尿病及其并发症的治疗提供了新的思路和方向。这些研究成果不仅丰富了我们对糖尿病病理生理的理解，也为临床医生在制定治疗方案时提供了重要的参考依据。

items.body:
原话：“Filmmaking is a tough business, and we are so grateful that our community has come together to back our project. It belongs just as much to Maitland as it does to Brendan and I.”
论点：独立电影制作如《Laundry Day》能够增强社区精神和创造力。

items.topic_zh: 独立电影制作对社区的影响
items.claim_zh: 独立电影制作如《Laundry Day》能够增强社区精神和创造力。
items.article_body:
Brendan Dennerley (33) and Matthew Collins (27) are proud to launch Laundry Day – the feature film debut of the new independent filmmaking collective Running Gag Reflex.
Laundry Day is an outrageous and slapstick take on 1980s creature features like Gremlins , Ghoulies , Critters , and The Blob . Matthew Collins, who also co-wrote and co-produced the film with Dennerley, stars as Billy, a lowly uni graduate who finds himself at the centre of a full-scale attack from killer sock puppets.
The project was filmed between across nine months at iconic locations across Maitland and Newcastle including Fort Scratchley, Maitland Repertory Theatre, and Maitland’s Family Hotel.
Over 50 locals supported the production either as performers, on-set technical crew, or additional support (including UK rapper Bigredcap, who produced an original song for the soundtrack).
Co-producer Matthew Collins says that indie productions such as Laundry Day do so much to build up community spirit and creativity.
“Filmmaking is a tough business, and we are so grateful that our community has come together to back our project. It belongs just as much to Maitland as it does to Brendan and I,” Mr Collins said.
Laundry Day premieres at 7pm on 24 October 2026 at Studio Amsterdam, Maitland.
items.title_zh: 地区电影制作人发起电影集体，首映《Laundry Day》
items.summary_zh: 独立电影《Laundry Day》的制作团队表示，电影制作是一项艰难的事业，感谢社区的支持使项目得以实现。团队成员强调，这部电影不仅属于他们个人，也属于梅特兰（Maitland）社区。文章论述了独立电影如何增强社区精神和创造力，指出社区的参与和支持对于电影项目的成功至关重要。通过集体努力，电影不仅成为艺术表达的载体，也促进了地方文化的繁荣与发展。
items.l1_lead: 独立电影《Laundry Day》的成功依赖于梅特兰社区的支持，强调了社区参与对电影制作和地方文化发展的重要性。
items.l2_summary:
独立电影《Laundry Day》的制作团队近日在梅特兰（Maitland）社区首映了这部作品，团队成员在发布会上表示，电影制作是一项充满挑战的事业，然而正是社区的支持使得这一项目得以顺利实现。他们强调，这部电影不仅是他们个人的创作，更是梅特兰社区的共同成果，体现了地方文化的独特性和活力。文章指出，独立电影在增强社区精神和创造力方面发挥了重要作用，社区的参与和支持对于电影项目的成功至关重要。

通过集体努力，电影不仅成为艺术表达的载体，还促进了地方文化的繁荣与发展。团队成员提到，电影制作的过程需要各方的协作与投入，正是这种集体的努力使得《Laundry Day》能够在艺术与文化的交汇点上取得成功。社区的参与不仅为电影注入了丰富的地方元素，也增强了居民之间的联系和归属感，进一步推动了社区的凝聚力。

总的来说，《Laundry Day》的成功不仅是制作团队的成就，更是梅特兰社区共同努力的结果。这部电影的首映不仅展示了独立电影的艺术价值，也彰显了社区在文化创作中的重要角色，提醒人们在追求艺术的同时，不应忽视社区的力量和支持。通过这样的合作，独立电影能够更好地反映地方特色，促进文化的多样性与繁荣。

items.title: Are GLP-1s the First Longevity Drugs? | Lifespan with Dr. David Sinclair - S2, Ep. 11（31:45）
items.body:
原话（31:45）：“I think GLP1s in history will be looked back as drugs that were originally found for diabetes and obesity, but will be taken by millions around the world for slowing down diseases of aging as well.”
论点：GLP-1药物不仅用于糖尿病和肥胖，还可能被广泛用于减缓衰老相关疾病。
论据：GLP-1药物在历史上将被视为减缓衰老疾病的药物。

items.title_zh: GLP-1药物或成首个长寿药物
items.summary_zh: 本文讨论了GLP-1（胰高血糖素样肽-1）药物的潜在作用，认为这些药物最初是为治疗糖尿病和肥胖而研发的，但未来可能会被全球数百万人用于减缓衰老相关疾病。科学家指出，GLP-1药物在历史上将被重新审视，作为减缓衰老疾病的重要药物。这一观点强调了GLP-1药物在延长健康寿命方面的潜力，预示着其在抗衰老领域的广泛应用。
items.l1_lead: GLP-1药物有望成为首个用于减缓衰老相关疾病的长寿药物，展现出延长健康寿命的潜力。
items.l2_summary:
GLP-1（胰高血糖素样肽-1）药物最初是为治疗糖尿病和肥胖而研发的，但近年来的研究表明，这些药物可能在延缓衰老相关疾病方面具有重要潜力。科学家们认为，GLP-1药物的作用不仅限于控制血糖和体重，还可能通过改善代谢健康和减少慢性疾病的风险，帮助全球数百万人减缓衰老过程。这一观点引发了对GLP-1药物的重新审视，认为它们可能成为未来抗衰老领域的重要药物。

研究显示，GLP-1药物能够通过多种机制影响身体的生理过程，包括促进胰岛素分泌、抑制胃排空和减少食欲，从而改善整体健康状况。此外，GLP-1药物还可能通过抗炎作用和改善心血管健康，进一步降低与衰老相关的疾病风险。这些发现为GLP-1药物在延长健康寿命方面的应用提供了科学依据，预示着其在未来可能被广泛用于抗衰老治疗。

总的来说，GLP-1药物的潜在作用超出了其原本的治疗目的，可能为人类健康和寿命的延长开辟新的方向。随着对这些药物研究的深入，未来可能会有更多的证据支持其在抗衰老领域的应用，进一步推动人们对健康老龄化的追求。

items.title_zh: GLP-1类药物是否是首个长寿药物？
items.summary_zh: 在一档节目中，科学家提出了一个观点，即衰老最终将被定义为一种疾病，这一转变将使医生能够开处方治疗衰老的药物，如GLP-1类药物（Glucagon-like peptide-1）。这一观点的核心在于，随着对衰老的重新定义，医疗行业将改变对衰老的看法，并推动相关药物的开发。这意味着未来可能会有更多针对衰老的治疗方案问世，从而改善人类的健康寿命。
items.l1_lead: 科学家认为，重新定义衰老为疾病将推动GLP-1类药物等治疗方案的发展，从而有望改善人类健康寿命。
items.l2_summary:
在一档节目中，科学家提出了一个颇具前瞻性的观点，即衰老可能最终会被重新定义为一种疾病。这一转变将为医生开处方治疗衰老的药物铺平道路，其中GLP-1类药物（Glucagon-like peptide-1）被认为是潜在的首个“长寿药物”。这一观点的核心在于，随着对衰老的理解不断深化，医疗行业将改变对衰老的传统看法，进而推动针对衰老的药物开发和治疗方案的出现。

GLP-1类药物最初是用于治疗2型糖尿病的，但研究表明它们在改善代谢健康、降低体重和延缓衰老相关疾病方面具有潜在的益处。这些药物通过模拟胰高血糖素样肽-1的作用，促进胰岛素分泌、抑制食欲，并改善心血管健康。随着科学家们对衰老机制的深入研究，GLP-1类药物的应用范围可能会进一步扩展，成为改善人类健康寿命的重要工具。

如果衰老被正式认定为一种疾病，医疗体系将可能会更加重视衰老相关的治疗方案，从而为患者提供更有效的干预措施。这不仅有助于延长人类的健康寿命，还可能减轻因衰老引发的各种慢性疾病的负担。未来，随着更多针对衰老的药物问世，医疗行业将迎来一场革命，改变人们对衰老的认知和应对方式。

总之，GLP-1类药物作为潜在的长寿药物，代表了医学界对衰老理解的重大进展。随着对衰老的重新定义，未来可能会有更多创新的治疗方案出现，进一步改善人类的生活质量和健康状况。

items.title: The South’s aging water infrastructure is getting pounded by climate change – fixing it is also a struggle
items.body: Extreme downpours and droughts, both fueled by rising global temperatures, are taking a toll. Communities trying to manage the threats face three big challenges.
items.attribution_basis: The Conversation 作者页 /profiles/john-c-morris-1526386（名+姓双命中）
items.title_zh: 南方老化水利基础设施受气候变化冲击，修复困难重重
items.summary_zh: 随着全球气温上升，极端降雨和干旱现象愈发频繁，给南方地区的水利基础设施带来了严峻挑战。社区在应对这些威胁时面临三大主要困难：基础设施老化、资金不足以及气候变化带来的不确定性。这些因素共同影响了水资源的管理和分配，迫使地方政府和相关机构不得不寻找有效的解决方案，以应对日益严峻的气候条件和基础设施的脆弱性。
items.l1_lead: 南方地区的老化水利基础设施在气候变化的影响下面临极端天气挑战，修复过程中遭遇资金不足和不确定性等多重困难。
items.l2_summary: 随着全球气温的上升，南方地区的水利基础设施正面临着气候变化带来的严峻挑战，尤其是极端降雨和干旱现象的频繁发生，使得这些基础设施的老化问题愈加突出。社区在应对这些气候威胁时，主要面临三大困难：首先是基础设施的老化，许多水利设施已经使用多年，亟需维修和升级，但由于缺乏足够的资金，修复工作进展缓慢。其次，资金不足使得地方政府和相关机构在进行必要的基础设施投资时捉襟见肘，无法有效应对日益严峻的气候条件。最后，气候变化带来的不确定性使得水资源的管理和分配变得更加复杂，地方政府在制定应对策略时面临诸多挑战。这些因素共同影响了水资源的有效管理，迫使相关机构不得不寻找创新和有效的解决方案，以应对基础设施的脆弱性和气候变化带来的压力。总的来说，南方地区的水利基础设施在气候变化的冲击下，修复和维护面临重重困难，亟需引起重视并采取切实可行的措施。
items.l3_translation:
气候变化正在威胁美国的水基础设施，愈演愈烈的风暴使社区遭受洪水侵袭，而干旱则在未做好准备的地区枯竭了淡水供应。

2024年4月，席卷南方的严重风暴展示了一些风险：在新奥尔良，降雨速度远远超过了城市的排水泵能够处理的速度。在密西西比州哈提斯堡附近，风暴期间一条水管破裂。其他社区则面临停电和在使用水之前需煮沸水以确保安全的通知。

我们研究基础设施的韧性和可持续性，看到危机正在加剧，特别是在美国东南部，老化的供水系统和雨水基础设施使更多社区面临风险，因为天气变得愈加极端。

为了找到最佳解决方案并建设韧性基础设施，社区需要认识到在变暖的世界中面临的威胁以及管理这些威胁的障碍。

水危机可能由水量过多或过少引起，并且可能以意想不到的方式挑战饮用水系统。

在过去十年中，阿拉巴马州北部和中部的部分地区经历了严重的干旱。此外，挖掘的水井因水位因干旱和过度使用而下降而干涸。

2023年，新奥尔良的水供应以另一种方式受到干旱的威胁：由于密西西比河的水流减缓，来自墨西哥湾的盐水侵入河流的范围比正常情况更远。

与此同时，暴雨事件越来越多地淹没雨水系统，威胁饮用水供应。随着全球气温上升，海洋变暖，这种温暖的水为强烈风暴提供了更多的水分。

密西西比州杰克逊市的情况就是极端情况的一个例子，该市人口近15万。杰克逊的供水系统在2022年之前就因泄漏和管道破裂而困扰了十多年，直到强烈的洪水淹没了系统，导致大多数居民数天内几乎没有水可用。

即使在洪水之前，杰克逊的居民也被建议在饮用水之前先煮沸。现在，借助8亿美元的联邦税款，维修工作正在进行，但关于如何在未来保持系统维护的问题仍然存在。4月的风暴再次袭击该地区，带来了破坏性的风、降雨和停电。

老化水基础设施的脆弱性在许多社区中显而易见。美国土木工程师学会在2021年的美国基础设施报告卡中估计，美国每两分钟就有一处水管破裂，每天损失60亿加仑的处理水。工程师们对美国市政供水系统的总体评分为C-。

洪水防护基础设施的评分甚至更低：美国的堤坝和水坝均获得D级，并警告说，扩展开发意味着更多的人和财产在下游，依赖堤坝和水坝的正常运作。

今天的基础设施从砖石建筑到电子网络不等——每种基础设施都有不同的需求、目标、责任和对气候变化的脆弱性。

此外，基础设施通常是相互依赖的。如果一个资产发生故障，例如管道或控制水处理厂的计算机系统，损害可能会蔓延到其他系统。例如，由于系统故障而排放到溪流中的未经处理的废水可能会影响下游社区的饮用水供应。

水问题跨越不同级别的政府、法律和法规，以及技术和学术专业知识，要求建立可能难以管理的合作伙伴关系。这可能导致不同政府机构之间的冲突，因为在监管控制和责任方面的争议，特别是在联邦、州和地方政府之间。

在许多地区，几个世纪以来建立的水基础设施塑造了随后的发展决策、可用资源和土地使用模式，包括新住宅、交通设施和商业的选址。

如今，这些基础设施也可能以其开发者从未想象过的方式受到气候变化的威胁。

更强烈的降雨事件使某些地区长期以来的洪水地图变得过时，而以前从未被认为有洪水风险的地区现在却经常发生洪水。这在沿海地区尤其如此，风暴可能伴随着异常高的潮汐、海平面上升和沉降。

关于谁为基础设施改善买单，或谁决定项目优先级的问题也可能引发冲突。

基础设施是昂贵的。单个项目，例如更换水管或处理设施，将涉及显著的设计和施工成本，以及许多贫困社区难以承担的维护和修理费用。

美国土木工程师学会在2021年估计，2020年代十年内所需的各类基础设施投资（5.9万亿美元）与计划和资金支持的基础设施工作（3.3万亿美元）之间的差距为2.6万亿美元。预计到2029年，仅饮用水和废水投资的年度缺口将达到4340亿美元。

建设新的气候韧性基础设施超出了许多社区，特别是低收入社区的财务能力。

联邦政府近年来采取了措施提供更多援助。2021年通过的《两党基础设施法》授权为饮用水、废水、水储存和水再利用项目提供550亿美元。随后一年通过的《通货膨胀削减法》包括5.5亿美元用于帮助弱势社区进行供水项目。

但这些资金并不能弥补缺口，减少联邦支出的政治压力使得未来联邦对基础设施的支持变得不确定。

地方社区、州和联邦机构需要重新审视来自老化基础设施的日益威胁。

items.title: Sewage testing robots process wastewater faster to predict COVID 19 outbreaks sooner
items.body: A community’s wastewater can predict coronavirus cases that haven’t yet been diagnosed. The quicker that information is known, the better.
items.attribution_basis: The Conversation 作者页 /profiles/rob-knight-1215921（名+姓双命中）
items.title_zh: 污水检测机器人加速处理废水以预测COVID-19疫情
items.summary_zh: 社区的废水可以预测尚未确诊的冠状病毒病例。通过污水检测（sewage testing），科学家能够更快地获取疫情信息，从而提前预警，帮助公共卫生部门采取相应措施。快速获取这些信息对于控制疫情传播至关重要。研究表明，及时的污水监测能够显著提高对COVID-19疫情的响应速度，进而减少感染人数和相关医疗负担。
items.l1_lead: 污水检测机器人能够快速获取疫情信息，帮助预测COVID-19病例，从而提高公共卫生响应速度，减少感染人数和医疗负担。
items.l2_summary: 污水检测（sewage testing）作为一种新兴的公共卫生监测手段，正在加速处理废水，以预测尚未确诊的冠状病毒病例。科学家们发现，通过对社区废水的分析，可以更快地获取疫情信息，从而为公共卫生部门提供提前预警。这种方法的关键在于其能够及时反映社区内病毒的传播情况，进而帮助相关部门采取相应的防控措施。研究表明，及时的污水监测能够显著提高对COVID-19疫情的响应速度，这对于控制疫情的传播至关重要。通过这种方式，公共卫生机构能够更有效地识别潜在的疫情爆发，从而减少感染人数和相关的医疗负担。因此，污水检测不仅为疫情监测提供了新的视角，也为公共卫生政策的制定提供了重要的数据支持，显示出其在应对公共卫生危机中的重要价值。
items.l3_translation:
研究简报是关于有趣学术工作的简短介绍。

通过使用污水处理机器人，我们的实验室能够以比非自动化的大规模系统快30倍的速度在废水中检测冠状病毒。这一进展发表在微生物学期刊《mSystems》上，为监测废水以获取COVID-19地方病例早期预警的社区提供了更多的提前时间。

当临床研究显示检测出SARS-CoV-2阳性的人在其粪便中排出病毒时，污水似乎是一个显而易见的寻找地点。废水监测可以在社区层面上用于在临床诊断之前查看潜在的疫情聚集，尤其是在COVID-19流行率远高于检测率的地区。

问题在于，由于许多人的浴室排水进入污水中，病毒在废水流中被严重稀释，更不用说他们冲走的其他垃圾。监测依赖于从废水中浓缩病毒颗粒，以检测这些低水平。这一步骤通常是废水分析中的主要瓶颈，因为它费时且劳动密集。我们的机器人系统采取了不同且更快速的方法。

全国各地的城市、学校和企业正在使用废水监测来发现周围的冠状病毒。

废水监测在高风险区域作为早期警报系统特别有用，例如在那些无证居民可能对个人检测保持谨慎的社区。

最常用的病毒浓缩技术使用过滤器，可能需要六到八小时才能将几十个污水样本转化为可以测试SARS-CoV-2存在的样本。我们的新协议在一次40分钟的运行中浓缩24个样本。

我们重新利用通常在实验室执行微生物学或细胞生物学任务的设备来处理污水。通过微型化和自动化我们的系统，我们消除了许多劳动密集的步骤、资源和相关成本。而且我们的无接触过程要快得多。

我们从圣地亚哥主要污水处理厂的自动取样器收集污水，以及从我们在加利福尼亚大学圣地亚哥分校校园内100多个检查井中部署的设备，这些设备每天每30分钟收集一次污水样本。

然后，在实验室中，我们不再依赖多个过滤步骤，而是使用微小的磁珠来富集病毒颗粒。我们购买了这些设计用于结合多种呼吸道病毒的纳米磁珠。污水处理机器人配备了一个专门的磁头，可以抓取附着有病毒的磁珠。它优先捕捉病毒颗粒，留下污水样本中的其他垃圾。

使用机器人自动化污水浓缩过程使我们能够在每个机器人中在40分钟内浓缩24个样本。然后同一台机器人可以提取病毒RNA，在36分钟内处理96个样本。最后，我们使用聚合酶链反应来搜索SARS-CoV-2的特征基因，类似于实验室对患者鼻拭子的临床诊断测试。

总体而言，我们的系统可以在4.5小时内处理96个样本，显著缩短从样本到结果的时间。

到目前为止，我们的研究是我们所知的唯一使用自动化过程的冠状病毒废水研究。

我们正在将这一技术作为校园大规模废水监测的一部分，每天在100多个地点进行取样。圣地亚哥学区也将其用作早期警报系统。

我们现在正在使用系统中的病毒基因组测序部分来追踪新SARS-CoV-2变种的出现。

items.title: What are the symptoms of omicron?
items.body: Omicron is continuing the trend set by delta, causing symptoms that resemble the common cold.
items.attribution_basis: The Conversation 作者页 /profiles/tim-spector-105795（名+姓双命中）
items.title_zh: 奥密克戎的症状是什么？
items.summary_zh: 奥密克戎（Omicron）继续延续德尔塔（Delta）变种的趋势，导致的症状与普通感冒相似。这一发现表明，奥密克戎感染者可能会出现流感样症状，如咳嗽、喉咙痛、流鼻涕等。这些症状的相似性可能会导致公众对其严重性的误解，因此了解这些症状对于及时识别和应对感染至关重要。科学家们强调，尽管症状相似，但仍需保持警惕，特别是在疫情持续的背景下。
items.l1_lead: 奥密克戎感染者的症状与普通感冒相似，可能导致公众对其严重性的误解，因此了解这些症状至关重要。
items.l2_summary: 奥密克戎（Omicron）变种的症状与普通感冒相似，这一发现延续了德尔塔（Delta）变种的趋势。研究表明，感染奥密克戎的患者可能会出现流感样症状，包括咳嗽、喉咙痛和流鼻涕等。这些症状的相似性可能导致公众对奥密克戎感染严重性的误解，因此，了解这些症状对于及时识别和应对感染至关重要。科学家们强调，尽管奥密克戎的症状与普通感冒相似，但在疫情持续的背景下，仍需保持警惕，以防止潜在的健康风险。总之，公众应提高对奥密克戎症状的认识，以便在出现相关症状时能够及时采取适当的防护措施。
items.l3_translation:
近两年来，数百万公众成员每天向ZOE COVID研究提交健康报告，帮助我们跟踪疫情的发展。特别是通过该研究应用程序提交的4.8亿份报告显示，随着病毒的演变，其引起的症状也在变化。

早在2020年，原始和阿尔法版本的冠状病毒迅速显现出三种非常常见的症状——咳嗽、发热和嗅觉丧失——以及至少20种其他症状。这些症状包括疲劳、头痛、呼吸急促、肌肉疼痛和胃肠问题，以及一些更不寻常的现象，如皮疹和“COVID舌”。

当德尔塔变种出现时，我们注意到最常报告的症状发生了变化。之前常见的症状，如呼吸急促、发热和嗅觉丧失，排名下降。感冒样症状——包括流鼻涕、喉咙痛和持续打喷嚏——变得更加普遍，尤其是在接种过疫苗的人群中，头痛和咳嗽也变得更加常见。

奥密克戎似乎延续了德尔塔所设定的趋势。它引起的症状更像是普通感冒，尤其是在接种过疫苗的人群中，系统性症状（如恶心、肌肉疼痛、腹泻和皮疹）则较少。

我们查看了在12月报告感染COVID的人们的健康报告，当时奥密克戎在英国传播，并将其与10月初的数据进行了比较，当时德尔塔是主要变种。我们还通过分析一小组被政府告知其阳性PCR结果被怀疑或确认是奥密克戎感染的贡献者的数据来验证我们的比较结果。

我们的分析显示，德尔塔和奥密克戎的整体症状特征没有显著差异，在这两个时间段内，排名前五的症状都是流鼻涕、头痛、疲劳、打喷嚏和喉咙痛。但在症状的整体流行程度上，存在一些明显的差异。

例如，嗅觉丧失（嗅觉或味觉丧失）在10月份排名前十，但现在已降至第17位。曾经是COVID的关键指标，现在仅在约五分之一的阳性检测者中出现。根据我们的数据，不到三分之一的人（29%）会经历发热，这也远低于我们过去看到的情况。

重要的是，我们发现只有一半的COVID患者出现了发热、咳嗽或嗅觉丧失这三种经典症状，这表明政府关于PCR检测的指导（建议如果出现这三种症状中的任何一种就应进行检测）已经严重过时。

这种新变种的传染性远高于之前的变种，导致英国及其他国家病例激增。尽管目前尚不清楚我们是否会面临因该疾病而导致的住院潮，但重要的是要记住，尽管对许多人来说，奥密克戎和德尔塔可能感觉像感冒，但它仍然可能致命或导致长期症状，影响日常生活，尤其是对于未接种疫苗或免疫系统受损的人群。

到目前为止，我们看到大多数病例出现在年轻人中，但随着整体感染率保持在如此高的水平，我们现在也看到老年人群体的病例上升。75岁以上人群中阳性病例的近期上升令人担忧，但我们希望英国老年人和更脆弱群体的高疫苗接种率将继续转化为较轻的症状和较少的住院病例。奥密克戎的主要问题更多是它在关键医疗人员中造成的缺勤潮。

随着我们在英国进入冬季的深处，周围出现了一些相当严重的感冒，以及常见的流感。ZOE COVID研究应用程序的数据告诉我们，目前COVID变种引起的症状与普通感冒非常相似。这意味着仅凭症状无法确定你得了什么。当COVID的传播率很高时，新的喉咙痛、流鼻涕或不寻常的疲劳应被视为COVID，直到你接受检测。

由于ZOE COVID研究应用程序的贡献者记录他们每天经历的任何症状以及任何COVID检测结果，我们还能够跟踪非COVID感冒的流行情况。就在三个月前，约每12个有新呼吸道症状的人中就有一个检测出COVID阳性。然而，随着奥密克戎的出现，目前约50%的“新感冒”实际上是COVID。

因此，如果你或家人感到不适，尤其是如果你经常流鼻涕和打喷嚏，很有可能是COVID。你应该待在家里并进行检测以确认。请记住，尽管快速检测（侧流检测）效果不错，尤其是如果你同时擦拭喉咙和鼻子，但它们的灵敏度低于PCR检测。当你进行一次检测时，尽量在接下来的几天重复进行，因为单次阴性的快速检测结果并不能保证你没有感染。

最后，无论政府的指导方针如何，无论你是否感染了COVID，如果你感到不适，尤其是出现奇怪或感冒样的症状，最好待在家里，避免接触他人，如果你外出，佩戴口罩，以避免将病菌传播给可能更脆弱的人。

匿名标题0，基因流行病学，伦敦国王学院

items.title: Should we all be using ‘sniff tests’ to screen for COVID 19?
items.body: Temperature checks have become a commonplace screening tool for COVID-19, but loss of sense of smell is a more predictive symptom of coronavirus infection than fever.
items.attribution_basis: The Conversation 作者页 /profiles/tim-spector-105795（名+姓双命中）
items.title_zh: 我们是否都应该使用“嗅觉测试”筛查COVID-19？
items.summary_zh: 温度检测已成为COVID-19的常见筛查工具，但失去嗅觉是比发热更具预测性的冠状病毒感染症状。研究表明，嗅觉丧失在COVID-19患者中更为普遍，且其出现时间通常早于其他症状。因此，嗅觉测试可能是一个有效的筛查方法，能够帮助更早地识别感染者，进而采取相应的防控措施。专家建议，在疫情防控中，结合嗅觉测试与温度检测，可能会提高筛查的准确性和效率。
items.l1_lead: 嗅觉测试在COVID-19筛查中比温度检测更具预测性，能更早识别感染者，建议结合使用以提高筛查准确性和效率。
items.l2_summary: 温度检测已成为COVID-19（新冠病毒）筛查的常见工具，但研究表明，嗅觉丧失（anosmia）是比发热（fever）更具预测性的冠状病毒感染症状。相关研究显示，嗅觉丧失在COVID-19患者中更为普遍，且其出现时间通常早于其他症状。这一发现提示我们，嗅觉测试可能成为一种有效的筛查方法，能够帮助更早地识别感染者，从而及时采取相应的防控措施。专家建议，在疫情防控中，结合嗅觉测试与温度检测，可能会显著提高筛查的准确性和效率。通过这种综合筛查方式，可以更好地应对疫情，降低传播风险，保护公众健康。因此，嗅觉测试的引入值得在实际防控中进行进一步的探索和应用。
items.l3_translation:
控制COVID-19传播的最佳方法之一是迅速识别感染冠状病毒的人，并防止他们将病毒传播给他人。

目前，体温检测被用作公共筛查工具，以识别COVID-19患者，像台湾这样的国家将体温检测作为其控制措施的关键组成部分。然而，几乎没有科学证据表明体温检测能够可靠地检测COVID-19。

首先，手持扫描仪仅测量皮肤温度，而不是核心体温，皮肤温度可能会有所波动，并且设备的可靠性存在问题。来自ZOE COVID症状研究应用程序的数据表明，超过一半（57%）的新冠病毒检测阳性者从未出现发热，而那些确实有体温升高的人平均只有两天的时间。机场的体温筛查未能检测到大多数感染者并不令人惊讶。

如果使用体温检测来检测COVID可能只提供一种虚假的安全感，那么我们应该做些什么呢？

来自我们应用程序400万用户的数据帮助我们确认，嗅觉丧失（嗅觉缺失）是4月份COVID-19的一个关键症状。我们为促使英国和其他国家将其作为官方症状做出了贡献。我的同事和我在《柳叶刀》上撰写的最新应用数据中强调，65%的COVID-19检测阳性成年人报告嗅觉丧失，其中相当一部分人从未经历过体温升高，而检测阳性的人中仅有40%多一点的人有发热。

对于大约16%的检测阳性者，嗅觉丧失是他们唯一的症状。重要的是，在COVID-19感染期间，嗅觉缺失持续约七天，通常更长，而大多数人的发热仅持续三天。

此外，伦敦大学学院的科学家进行的一项研究表明，在病毒第一波期间，超过75%报告嗅觉丧失的人检测出冠状病毒抗体，尽管其中四分之一的人没有表现出其他经典症状。

总体而言，数据表明，嗅觉的突然丧失是COVID-19的一个更常见的早期症状，尤其是在所有年龄组中。对于年轻人来说，它是检测COVID-19阳性的20倍更好的预测指标，而对于老年人来说，是13倍更好的指标，优于任何其他症状。

基于这些发现，在机场和酒店等场所使用“嗅觉测试”而不是体温检测可能是更好的广泛筛查方法。虽然从理论上看这是个好主意，但不幸的是，这里有一个问题。

首先，嗅觉减退是相当常见的。近20%的成年人有某种程度的嗅觉丧失，而这一数字在75岁以上的人群中上升到80%。这些人不太可能有任何证明其先前嗅觉丧失的证据，以使他们免于嗅觉测试的限制。

其次，当我们查看应用程序的数据时，我们发现大多数人在感染COVID-19后大约需要一周的时间才能恢复嗅觉。但大约十分之一的人嗅觉丧失持续三周或更长时间，远远超过他们可能具有传染性的时间。

最后，许多人在因普通感冒、鼻窦炎或花粉症而鼻塞时会失去嗅觉。尽管鼻塞不被视为COVID-19的症状，但简单的嗅觉测试可能无法区分这两者。

这意味着，尽管嗅觉测试可能在感染时识别出COVID-19患者，但也会有大量非传染性的人同样未能通过测试，并面临不必要的限制。

因此，尽管“嗅觉测试”可能不是答案，但嗅觉的突然变化仍然可能是早期COVID-19感染的最佳指示。我们的应用显示这一症状在儿童中较少见，但这可能是因为他们不太可能注意到，除非经过测试。

检查嗅觉变化很简单，可以每天在家中使用简单的香味家居物品，如咖啡、柠檬、香草或臭奶酪进行。如果您发现自己或孩子的嗅觉发生了任何突然变化，而这种变化对您来说并不正常，您应该自我隔离并尽快进行COVID-19检测。

ZOE COVID症状研究应用程序可以从苹果应用商店和谷歌Play商店下载。研究更新和数据可以在covid.joinzoe.com/找到。

伦敦国王学院的遗传流行病学教授

某某人从多个来源获得资助，包括威康信托、医学研究理事会、国家健康研究院、CDRF、Seerave基金会、达能、ZOE、BHF。ZOE CSS应用程序是非营利性项目。他是ZOE全球有限公司的联合创始人，并且是两本关于营养的书的作者；《饮食神话》（Orion 2016）和《被喂养的真相 - 我们关于食物的许多说法都是错误的》（某某人 2020）。

伦敦国王学院作为《对话》英国的成员提供资金支持。

items.title: Why one size fits all diets don’t work – new study
items.attribution_basis: The Conversation 作者页 /profiles/tim-spector-105795（名+姓双命中）
items.title_zh: 为何“一刀切”的饮食方案无效——新研究揭示
items.summary_zh: 一项新研究探讨了“一刀切”饮食方案为何对不同个体无效。研究指出，个体的基因、微生物组、代谢率等因素对饮食反应有显著影响。通过对参与者的饮食习惯和生理反应进行分析，研究发现相同的饮食在不同人群中可能导致不同的健康结果。关键证据表明，个体化饮食方案能够更有效地促进健康和减重，而非普遍适用的饮食模式。研究结论强调，未来的营养指导应更加注重个体差异，以实现更好的健康效果。
items.l1_lead: 研究表明，个体的基因和代谢差异使得“一刀切”的饮食方案无效，个性化饮食更能促进健康和减重。
items.l2_summary:
一项新研究探讨了“一刀切”饮食方案为何对不同个体无效，揭示了个体差异在饮食反应中的重要性。研究指出，个体的基因、微生物组（microbiome）、代谢率等因素对饮食反应有显著影响，这意味着相同的饮食在不同人群中可能导致不同的健康结果。通过对参与者的饮食习惯和生理反应进行分析，研究发现，普遍适用的饮食模式往往无法满足每个人的需求，导致减重和健康改善的效果不尽如人意。

关键证据表明，个体化饮食方案能够更有效地促进健康和减重。研究强调，未来的营养指导应更加注重个体差异，以实现更好的健康效果。这一发现挑战了传统的饮食建议，提示我们在制定饮食计划时，需考虑每个人的独特生理特征和生活方式，而非简单地推广一种适用于所有人的饮食方案。通过个体化的营养干预，能够更精准地满足个体的健康需求，从而提高饮食干预的成功率和有效性。总之，这项研究为未来的营养科学提供了新的视角，强调了个体化饮食的重要性。
items.l3_translation:
冠状病毒大流行使健康问题成为许多人关注的焦点。虽然避免 COVID-19 的最佳方法是首先不感染病毒，但我们开始理解为什么有些人会因该疾病而严重生病，而其他人则只有轻微或没有症状。

年龄和虚弱是严重 COVID-19 的最重要风险因素，但我们 COVID 症状研究应用程序的数据（近四百万人使用）显示，与饮食相关的疾病，如肥胖、心脏病和 2 型糖尿病，是导致住院的重要风险因素。

在英国，约三分之一的成年人肥胖，更多的人超重。在美国，约五分之二的成年人和近五分之一的儿童肥胖。从政府的营养指南到 Instagram 上的时尚饮食，关于如何减肥的建议层出不穷。显然，这些方法并没有奏效。

这是一个复杂的问题。性别、种族、社会经济状况和健康食品的可获得性等因素都起着作用。但在个体层面上，我们对每个人应该如何饮食以优化健康和体重的理解仍然相对有限。

为了寻找答案，我们伦敦国王学院的研究团队与麻省总医院、斯坦福大学和健康科学公司 ZOE 的同事们共同发起了 PREDICT，这是世界上最大的持续营养研究。我们的第一批结果现已发表在《自然医学》上。

PREDICT-1 是 PREDICT 研究计划的第一阶段，涉及超过 1000 名成年人（包括数百对双胞胎），他们在两周内持续监测，以发现他们对不同食物的反应。

参与者在医院进行了一天的初步设置，以进行详细的血液测量和进食经过精心设计的定量餐后的反应测试。然后，他们在家中进行研究，遵循设定的餐食和自己的自由选择食物的时间表。我们测量了从血糖、脂肪、胰岛素和炎症水平到运动、睡眠和肠道细菌（微生物组）多样性等一系列营养反应和健康指标。

这种详细的持续分析得益于可穿戴技术的使用。这些技术包括连续血糖监测仪和数字活动追踪器，使我们能够全天候跟踪参与者的血糖和活动水平。简单的指尖采血测试也使我们能够定期测量他们的血脂水平。

所有这些测量加起来形成了数百万个数据点，需要使用复杂的机器学习技术（人工智能的一种）进行分析，以发现模式并做出预测。

我们首先注意到的是，即使是同卵双胞胎，对相同餐食的个体胰岛素、血糖和血脂反应存在广泛的差异。例如，一个双胞胎可能对摄入碳水化合物有健康的反应，但对脂肪则没有，而另一个双胞胎则正好相反。这立即告诉我们，每个人都是独特的，没有一种完美的饮食或正确的饮食方式适合所有人。

观察到遗传因素在决定我们对食物反应中的作用仅占小部分，也告诉我们，声称能确定“适合你基因的饮食”的简单基因测试是无效且具有误导性的。有趣的是，同卵双胞胎仅共享约三分之一的相同肠道微生物种类，这可能有助于解释营养反应中的一些差异，并且指向通过操控微生物组来改善健康和体重的机会。

我们还发现，餐食的时间以个性化的方式影响营养反应。同一餐在早餐时与午餐时的营养反应可能不同。但在其他人身上则没有差异，这打破了“所有人都有正确的用餐时间”这一神话。

另一个惊喜是发现，餐食在卡路里、脂肪、碳水化合物、蛋白质和纤维（宏量营养素或“宏”）方面的组成对营养反应也有高度个性化的影响。例如，有些人对碳水化合物的处理能力优于脂肪，而其他人则相反。因此，基于固定卡路里计数或宏量营养素比例的处方饮食过于简单，不适合所有人。

然而，尽管参与者之间存在广泛的变异性，每个人对在不同日子相同时间进食的相同餐食的反应却出奇一致。这使得根据对其基础代谢的了解来预测某人对任何食物的反应成为可能。

有趣的是，我们发现血液中炎性分子的水平变化可达十倍，即使在看似健康的人群中，这些炎症标志物的升高与对脂肪的不健康反应相关联。

我们使用“饮食炎症”一词来指代这些在进食后触发的不健康代谢效应。反复经历由过量血糖和脂肪反应引起的饮食炎症与心脏病、2 型糖尿病、非酒精性脂肪肝病和肥胖等疾病的风险增加相关。

从积极的角度来看，我们的研究结果表明，通过以更个性化的方式进食，旨在避免在餐后触发不健康的炎症反应，可能有助于改善体重管理和长期健康。

在体重问题上，我们传统上过于强调我们无法控制的因素，尤其是遗传。事实是，虽然遗传起着作用，但还有许多更重要的因素影响我们的代谢、体重和健康。是时候摆脱过于笼统的指导方针、时尚饮食和一刀切的计划，发展更个性化、科学的营养方法。

items.title: Coronavirus: research reveals way to predict infection – without a test
items.body: Symptoms like loss of smell and taste are powerful predictors of COVID-19 infections.
items.attribution_basis: The Conversation 作者页 /profiles/tim-spector-105795（名+姓双命中）
items.title_zh: 新研究揭示无检测预测新冠感染的方法
items.summary_zh: 研究表明，失去嗅觉和味觉等症状是COVID-19感染的强有力预测指标。这项研究强调了通过观察这些症状来预测感染的潜力，可能为公共卫生监测提供新的思路。通过分析大量病例数据，研究人员发现，嗅觉和味觉的丧失在感染者中普遍存在，且与病毒的传播密切相关。这一发现为早期识别感染者提供了可能的途径，减少了对检测资源的依赖，尤其在疫情高发时期。研究结果可能对未来的疫情应对策略产生重要影响。
items.l1_lead: 研究发现，失去嗅觉和味觉是COVID-19感染的强有力预测指标，可能为公共卫生监测提供新的思路，减少对检测资源的依赖。
items.l2_summary:
一项新研究揭示了通过观察失去嗅觉和味觉等症状来预测新冠病毒（COVID-19）感染的潜力。这些症状被认为是感染的强有力预测指标，研究强调了其在公共卫生监测中的应用价值。研究人员通过分析大量病例数据，发现嗅觉和味觉的丧失在感染者中普遍存在，且与病毒的传播密切相关。这一发现为早期识别感染者提供了新的可能性，尤其是在疫情高发时期，能够减少对检测资源的依赖。

具体而言，研究表明，失去嗅觉和味觉的症状在COVID-19感染者中具有显著的普遍性，这意味着这些症状可以作为一种有效的筛查工具，帮助公共卫生部门更快速地识别潜在的感染者。通过这种方法，公共卫生监测可以在不依赖大量检测资源的情况下，及时发现和控制疫情的传播。这一研究结果不仅为当前疫情应对提供了新的思路，也可能对未来应对类似疫情的策略产生深远影响。

总的来说，这项研究为我们理解COVID-19的传播机制提供了重要的线索，同时也为公共卫生政策的制定提供了科学依据，强调了症状监测在疫情管理中的重要性。
items.l3_translation:
英国和一些美国州已经制定了放松冠状病毒封锁的计划。最终，任何试图放松限制的政府都必须密切关注每日感染人数和病毒传播情况。理想情况下，每一个新病例都应该被追踪和管理。

问题在于，大多数国家缺乏足够的资源来测试和追踪足够多的人。但我们的应用程序，名为COVID症状研究，基于大约340万用户在英国、美国和瑞典每日记录症状的数据，可能会有所帮助。在一项发表在《自然医学》上的新研究中，我们展示了该应用程序可以仅根据症状估计某人是否感染了COVID-19，并且准确度很高。

该应用程序（以前称为COVID症状追踪器）由我们在伦敦国王学院的团队与健康科技公司ZOE（我们中的一位共同创办）合作于3月推出。用户每天被要求报告他们是否感觉良好或是否有与COVID-19相关的症状。在14天内，在社交媒体的帮助下，我们收集了200万用户的数据，获取了关于冠状病毒感染症状和疾病在英国传播的重要信息。

在我们这项经过同行评审的新研究中，我们分析了来自英国的近250万人在应用程序中定期记录健康状态的数据。大约三分之一的人记录了与COVID-19相关的多种症状。超过15,000人报告曾接受冠状病毒检测，其中近6,500人检测呈阳性。我们通过来自约168,000名美国用户的数据确认了这些发现——其中2,736人接受了COVID-19检测，726人检测呈阳性。美国用户大约在英国用户之后一周开始参与。

接着，我们调查了哪些已知与COVID-19相关的症状最有可能预测阳性检测结果。味觉和嗅觉丧失特别显著，检测出冠状病毒感染的用户中有三分之二报告了这些症状，而检测阴性的参与者中仅有五分之一多一点。

然后，我们创建了一个数学模型，可以根据个人的年龄、性别和四个关键症状的组合（嗅觉或味觉丧失、严重或持续咳嗽、疲劳和跳过餐食）以近80%的准确率预测个体是否可能感染COVID-19。

这具有巨大的意义：在缺乏广泛、可靠的冠状病毒检测的情况下，通过应用程序记录症状是一种简单、快速且具有成本效益的方法，可以帮助人们了解自己是否可能被感染，并采取自我隔离和检测的措施。

我们现在正在通过与英国卫生和社会护理部的冠状病毒检测计划合作，进一步验证我们的预测模型，为每周报告新症状的数千名应用程序用户提供拭子检测。在美国，我们计划开展研究，部署抗体检测，以查看过去报告症状的人是否确实感染了病毒，以及抗体是否足以保护他们免受再次感染。

重要的是，我们的结果表明，味觉或嗅觉丧失是COVID-19感染的一个关键早期警告信号。食欲减退和严重疲劳的表现也优于咳嗽和发热等经典症状。仅关注咳嗽和发热将会漏掉许多病例。尽管世界卫生组织和美国疾病控制与预防中心最近扩大了症状列表，但许多政府，如英国，改变的速度却很慢。英格兰国家健康服务（NHS）仍在其网站上将咳嗽和发热列为主要症状。

我们强烈敦促各国政府和卫生当局扩大症状范围，并建议任何经历突然嗅觉或味觉丧失的人假设自己感染了病毒，并遵循当地的自我隔离指南。

正在收集的详细症状数据向我们展示了病毒临床表现的巨大多样性，以至于我们开始随着时间的推移定义出具有不同结果和持续时间的不同簇。例如，快速出现的多种症状的预后优于那些缓慢出现的、伴有疲劳和胸部症状的情况。

我们还发现许多人症状反复出现，持续超过一个月。与大多数政府在某种程度上进行的检测和接触追踪相结合，COVID症状研究应用程序是帮助各国更安全地解除封锁的潜在工具。这一点尤其重要，因为检测资源将继续稀缺。从尽可能多的人那里收集详细的健康数据是这一过程的一个重要部分，同时确保充分尊重同意和隐私。

这种数据驱动的方法依赖于数百万人使用该应用程序每天记录他们的健康状况。即使在我们恢复正常生活时，我们也需要保持警惕——人们需要了解完整的症状范围。我们呼吁人们下载该应用程序，并养成每天花一分钟时间进行检查的习惯。该应用程序得到了慈善机构以及威尔士和苏格兰政府的认可和推广——但尚未得到英格兰国家健康服务的认可。

COVID症状研究应用程序及其他类似应用程序的快速推出证明了此类应用程序在应对疫情时进行实时流行病学研究的价值。该应用程序在研究中还有更大的作用。

我们与美国麻省总医院的大型团队以及慈善机构“抵抗癌症”合作，正在产生关于肥胖、高血压药物和社会剥夺等国家间风险因素的早期数据。我们还在研究对医疗工作者的风险。这些工作中的一些尚未经过同行评审，即专家相互审查对方工作的过程。

COVID症状研究应用程序可以从Apple App Store和Google Play Store下载。

items.title: Coronavirus: how to keep your gut microbiome healthy to fight COVID 19
items.body: Your gut plays an important role in building your immune defences. Don’t neglect it.
items.attribution_basis: The Conversation 作者页 /profiles/tim-spector-105795（名+姓双命中）
items.title_zh: 新冠病毒：如何保持肠道微生物群健康以抵抗COVID-19
items.summary_zh: 肠道在构建免疫防御中发挥着重要作用，因此保持肠道微生物群（gut microbiome）的健康至关重要。研究表明，肠道微生物群的多样性与免疫系统的功能密切相关，健康的肠道微生物群能够增强机体对病毒的抵抗力，包括新冠病毒（SARS-CoV-2）。通过合理饮食、摄入益生菌和益生元等方式，可以有效维护肠道微生物的平衡，从而提升免疫力。总之，关注肠道健康是应对COVID-19的重要策略之一。
items.l1_lead: 保持肠道微生物群健康通过合理饮食和益生菌摄入，可以增强免疫力，有助于抵抗新冠病毒。
items.l2_summary:
新冠病毒（SARS-CoV-2）的流行使得人们对免疫系统的关注日益增加，而肠道微生物群（gut microbiome）在构建免疫防御中扮演着重要角色。研究表明，肠道微生物群的多样性与免疫系统的功能密切相关，健康的肠道微生物群能够显著增强机体对病毒的抵抗力，包括新冠病毒。具体而言，维持肠道微生物的平衡不仅有助于提升免疫力，还能改善整体健康状况。

为了有效维护肠道微生物群的健康，合理饮食是关键。摄入富含纤维的食物，如水果、蔬菜和全谷物，可以促进有益菌的生长。此外，益生菌（probiotics）和益生元（prebiotics）的摄入也被认为是维护肠道健康的重要手段。益生菌是指能够提供健康益处的活微生物，而益生元则是指能够促进益生菌生长的非消化性食物成分。通过这些方式，可以有效提升肠道微生物的多样性，从而增强免疫系统的功能。

总之，关注肠道健康不仅是提升免疫力的有效策略，也是应对COVID-19的重要措施之一。随着对肠道微生物群与免疫系统关系的深入研究，未来可能会有更多针对肠道健康的干预措施被提出，以帮助人们更好地抵御新冠病毒及其他病毒的侵袭。
items.l3_translation:
这些是前所未有的时期。新冠病毒SARS-CoV-2引起的COVID-19（新冠肺炎）已被世界卫生组织正式宣布为全球大流行。许多国家已封闭边界，并将民众置于自愿或强制的封锁状态。文化和体育活动已被取消或推迟——包括2020年欧洲足球锦标赛和格拉斯顿伯里音乐节——酒吧和餐馆关闭，人们开始抢购卫生纸和意大利面等生活必需品。尽管情况可能让人感觉失控，但仍有许多事情可以做，以保护自己和周围人的健康。

首先，遵循国家关于预防COVID-19的指导：通过定期洗手、避免触摸面部和减少社交接触来避免传播病毒并降低感染的机会。这对于保护高风险群体尤为重要，包括已有健康状况的人、老年人和孕妇。

除了从外部保护自己免受病毒侵害外，您还可以通过增强免疫系统来从内部增强防御能力。许多人，尤其是年轻人，发展出的疾病通常非常轻微。免疫系统复杂且对周围环境高度敏感，因此许多因素会影响其功能并不令人惊讶。重要的是要知道，这些因素大多数并不是在我们的基因中硬编码的，而是受到生活方式和周围环境的影响。

您可以立即控制的一件事是肠道中数万亿微生物的健康，这些微生物统称为微生物组。最近的研究表明，肠道微生物组在身体对感染的免疫反应和维持整体健康方面发挥着至关重要的作用。健康的肠道微生物组不仅能对抗冠状病毒等感染性病原体，还能帮助防止可能危害健康的免疫过度反应，这些反应会损害肺部和其他重要器官。这些过度的免疫反应可能导致呼吸衰竭和死亡。（这也是为什么我们应该谈论“支持”而不是“增强”免疫系统，因为过度活跃的免疫反应可能和免疫反应不足一样危险。）

与其服用声称“增强免疫系统”的补充剂而没有良好的支持证据，不如关注您所吃的食物对肠道微生物种类和数量的影响。多样化的微生物组是健康的微生物组，包含许多不同的物种，每种物种在免疫和健康中都发挥着作用。随着年龄的增长，微生物组的多样性会下降，这可能有助于解释我们在免疫反应中看到的一些与年龄相关的变化，因此在整个生命中维持健康的微生物组显得尤为重要。

肠道微生物组与免疫系统之间的相互作用的细节尚未完全理解。但似乎微生物组的组成与炎症之间存在联系——炎症是免疫反应的一个标志。肠道细菌产生许多有益的化学物质，还能激活食物中的维生素A，这有助于调节免疫系统。

增加微生物组多样性的最佳方法是食用多种植物性食物，这些食物富含纤维，同时限制超加工食品，包括垃圾食品。遵循地中海饮食也已被证明可以改善肠道微生物组的多样性并减少炎症：多吃水果、蔬菜、坚果、种子和全谷物；健康脂肪如高质量的特级初榨橄榄油；以及瘦肉或鱼。避免酒精、盐、糖果和含糖饮料，以及人造甜味剂或其他添加剂。

如果您在自我隔离或隔离期间担心获取新鲜农产品，冷冻水果、浆果和蔬菜与新鲜的同样健康，并且能比目前推荐的两周隔离期保存更长时间。罐装水果、豆类和豆荚是另一种持久的选择。

您还可以通过定期食用天然酸奶和手工奶酪来支持您的微生物组，这些食品含有活性微生物（益生菌）。另一种天然益生菌的来源是富含细菌和酵母的饮料，如克非尔（发酵牛奶）或康普茶（发酵茶）。发酵的蔬菜类食品，如韩国泡菜（和德国酸菜）也是一个不错的选择。

无论您是为自己、家人还是年长的亲戚或朋友购物，选择支持健康肠道微生物组的食物远比囤积卫生纸重要。管理您的心理健康、保持身体活动和获得足够的睡眠也将有助于保持免疫系统的良好状态。别忘了洗手！

要了解更多关于肠道微生物组重要性的信息，请收听《为您而制的医学》，这是《蚁丘》播客关于医疗保健未来及其如何变得更加个性化的系列节目。在这里收听或在您获取播客的地方订阅《蚁丘》。

伦敦国王学院的遗传流行病学匿名标题0

匿名人员1从包括医学研究委员会、威康信托、国家健康研究院、CDRF、达能、Zoe Global在内的多个来源获得学术资助。他是精准营养公司Zoe Global LTD的联合创始人。
他从两本流行科学书籍《饮食神话》（Orion 2016）和《喂养》（匿名人员2 2020）中获得版税。

伦敦国王学院作为《对话UK》的成员提供资金支持。

撰写文章并加入一个由超过234,700名来自5,633个机构的学者和研究人员组成的不断壮大的社区。
